subject: 600 kW Per Rack: The AI Power Crisis Reshaping Electrical Infrastructure
body:
# 600 kW Per Rack: The AI Power Crisis Reshaping Electrical Infrastructure

> ## **TL;DR — Five things to know**
>
>
> 1. AI racks go from 120 kW today to 600 kW by 2027. Power infrastructure value per rack jumps from $36K to $398K+ — more than 10× baseline. This is not incremental.
>
> 2. The architecture shifts completely — AC→50V DC becomes AC→800V DC (HVDC). Silicon Carbide and GaN are the enabling materials. NVIDIA has already picked its semiconductor partners.
>
> 3. Air cooling is effectively dead above 40 kW. The liquid cooling market grows from $5.5B to $25.8B by 2035. Every new hyperscale campus is being designed liquid-native from the ground up.
>
> 4. Power transformers now carry 4-year lead times. More than 50% of U.S. data centers planned for 2026 face delays. This is a structural bottleneck, not a supply chain hiccup.
>
> 5. The investment thesis spans five layers: grid infrastructure → facility power → rack PSU → power semiconductors → chip-level VRM. Each has different risk, margin, and timing.

## **Five Generations. Five Times the Power. Twenty-Four Months.**

A GB200 Blackwell rack today draws 120 kilowatts. That’s already forcing hyperscale operators to redesign power distribution floors and pull in supplemental cooling hardware mid-build. GB300 takes that to 140 kW. Vera Rubin, shipping in 2026, clears 200 kW. Vera Rubin CPX hits 380 kW. And Vera Rubin Ultra — paired with NVIDIA’s new Kyber rack architecture — lands at 600 kW per rack.

[![](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!c0rv!,w_1100,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F40a4d418-e10e-4b29-9401-bf4503f266f9_2186x1068.png)](https://substack.com/redirect/d4ca9b76-1146-40be-8bf6-de2e821bab24?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

Six hundred kilowatts. In a single rack. Roughly the power draw of 600 American homes, packed into a steel enclosure seven feet tall and two feet wide. A **1,000-rack** AI cluster at Vera Rubin Ultra density requires 600 megawatts of utility-grade power — the average electrical load of San Francisco.

The economic consequence, per Morgan Stanley Research, is equally direct. Power infrastructure value per AI server rack jumps from **$36,000 with GB200** to **$398,160 with Vera Rubin CPX** — a 1,005% increase — and exceeds 10× baseline with Vera Rubin Ultra. The power electronics industry isn’t a side story in the AI buildout. It’s one of the central economic narratives.

[![](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!Gd9E!,w_1100,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Fbba815e1-abab-4305-92ca-02e4f0fe16d2_1019x390.jpeg)](https://substack.com/redirect/330c46f5-fd92-40d1-ad02-05f60a70ad7b?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

###### Source: Morgan Stanley Research, Exhibit 7

## **The Architecture Has to Change. Completely.**

Today’s data centers run on a power architecture that was never designed for what’s being asked of it. AC from the grid converts to low-voltage DC inside each server’s PSU. Fine at 10 kW per rack — a number that grew only incrementally for decades. Now it’s growing exponentially, and at 600 kW the physics turn against you hard.

[![](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!S6zs!,w_1100,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F56235366-2d97-4835-acf2-659e0a1dca92_1868x1178.png "")](https://substack.com/redirect/dfcbfb79-6f5b-4618-ae62-cfd838f97ac7?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

###### Source: AEIS

The problem is Ohm’s law. Power loss in a conductor equals current squared times resistance (P = I²R). Low-voltage DC forces you to move the same wattage at much higher current, and losses scale with the *square* of that current. The copper in your busways heats up. The conversion stages

[![](https://substackcdn.com/image/youtube/w_728,c_limit/l_youtube_play_qyqt8q,w_120/r_wEyPgabnU)](https://substack.com/redirect/aff5ce97-860e-4e45-85e3-c4a0ab2e388f?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

[Andrew Song](https://substack.com/redirect/cd1dadde-169c-47d9-9554-94ea7e8a90cd?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) is the co-founder of [Make Sunsets](https://substack.com/redirect/40f96c75-5758-4b1a-8b99-a2753ab37cda?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ), a climate startup working to slow global warming by deploying reflective aerosols in the stratosphere. A longtime startup operator, Andrew has spent his career taking contrarian paths, from early work in AI to now building one of the most debated climate interventions in the world. At Make Sunsets, he focuses on translating complex science into practical action, raising capital through unconventional channels, and pushing forward a mission-driven company designed to buy humanity time as temperatures rise.

*Listen now on **[Youtube](https://substack.com/redirect/aff5ce97-860e-4e45-85e3-c4a0ab2e388f?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ), [Spotify](https://substack.com/redirect/8ed83c42-4a69-4705-b7db-84dd0c2e7c2b?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) or [Apple Podcasts](https://substack.com/redirect/d2f45981-1150-486a-9a29-d65be4e06c27?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)***

But Andrew’s most demanding role is being a full-time single dad to his two young sons. After gaining sole custody due to their mother’s struggles with bipolar disorder, Andrew has learned to navigate parenting, entrepreneurship, and mental health advocacy all at once. Living in the Bay Area near extended family, he relies on community, resilience, and regimented prioritization to raise his boys while building a startup on hard mode. We discussed:

* **Why climate change became personal:** How Andrew’s motivation to cool the planet is rooted in building a safer future for his kids.
* **Building a startup on hard mode:** What it’s like to raise venture capital, run a climate company, and be a full-time single dad at the same time.
* **Navigating mental health and custody:** Andrew’s experience gaining sole custody of his sons and why normalizing conversations around mental illness matters.
* **Creating a village of support:** How living near family and leaning on community makes single parenting and entrepreneurship possible.
* **Choosing purpose over comfort:** Why Andrew believes it’s possible to live modestly in the Bay Area while prioritizing meaningful work.
* **Raising resilient, curious kids:** From RV road trips to using AI as a learning tool, how Andrew encourages independence, curiosity, and grit at home.

**Where to find Andrew Song**

# [AINews] The Two Sides of OpenClaw

In an opportune coinciding of big three letter conferences, the [TED talk](https://substack.com/redirect/140de1de-9d8c-4a2d-8e64-e8f8395d1ff5?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) and the [AIE talks](https://substack.com/redirect/940cfdb8-2623-415a-9349-90fb95558858?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) of Peter Steinberger dropped today. To the general public, the inspiring story of OpenClaw was delightfully [told onstage](https://substack.com/redirect/48752db4-dbc5-4594-9468-13a3fae33a5c?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ), which recaps all the highs:

[![](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!w4xU!,w_1100,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Fd938eb29-488f-4a91-9b9d-7ba5dabf55af_1416x1022.png)](https://substack.com/redirect/8ad8b935-5f8d-4814-90f6-6137a2f95bfb?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

To the engineering audience, it was more sober, talking about the unprecedented levels of security incidents (60x more reports than curl, at least 20% of skill contributions malicious) and scaling issues involved in maintaining the fastest growing open source project in history:

[![](https://substackcdn.com/image/youtube/w_728,c_limit/l_youtube_play_qyqt8q,w_120/zgNvts_2TUE)](https://substack.com/redirect/a48b0aa2-e92d-4e88-979f-a06ac20ab0bb?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

An AMA moderated by me is included at the end.

Contrast them, thoughts welcome.

> AI News for 4/16/2026-4/17/2026. We checked 12 subreddits, [544 Twitters](https://substack.com/redirect/2b8cdbf6-d0c0-44ee-b893-689af41dd0ef?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) and no further Discords. [AINews’ website](https://substack.com/redirect/ae2b351b-9cf6-45e7-89de-a6f66b373bbc?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) lets you search all past issues. As a reminder, [AINews is now a section of Latent Space](https://substack.com/redirect/3d89158f-93aa-4750-9ddd-9b009081f798?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ). You can [opt in/out](https://substack.com/redirect/c5214766-9057-4e66-bdf2-d24f7ca996cd?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) of email frequencies!

---

**Anthropic’s Claude Opus 4.7 and Claude Design rollout**

* **Claude Design launched as Anthropic’s first design/prototyping surface**: [@claudeai](https://substack.com/redirect/fed005bc-0959-4112-8950-60c67b648f23?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) announced **Claude Design**, a research-preview tool for generating prototypes, slides, and one-pagers from natural-language instructions, powered by **Claude Opus 4.7**. The launch immediately framed Anthropic as moving beyond chat/coding into design tooling; multiple observers called it a direct shot at **Figma/Lovable/Bolt/v0**, including [@Yuchenj\_UW](https://substack.com/redirect/36fa055a-72fb-4a18-9f18-b0652fc92fea?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ), [@kimmonismus](https://substack.com/redirect/d50187fc-a11b-407e-8cac-5faf848dcd5f?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ), and [@skirano](https://substack.com/redirect/44bbcbaa-f8d6-4009-b5c2-918422b07663?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ). The market reaction itself became part of the story, with [@Yuchenj\_UW](https://substack.com/redirect/063952cf-9f1f-4665-9cbe-e97cd72a7af6?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) and others noting Figma’s sharp drawdown after the announcement. Product details surfaced via [@TheRundownAI](https://substack.com/redirect/f0a6dbea-fdca-42e2-844d-722ab2e24b50?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ): inline refinement, sliders, exports to **

subject: Generalizable robots in the next 3–4 years
body:
# Generalizable robots in the next 3–4 years

Hello, fellow humans! I’m sharing some of the most interesting conversations I’ve had recently about progress in AI research and the emergence of consciousness in AI systems.

I recently spoke with **Danijar Hafner**, who until recently was a staff researcher at **Google DeepMind.** He’s now on a new journey, having founded a new company. We discussed AI research and world models that Danijar has worked on in the past.

**Key moments from our conversation:**

* Architecture is not that important for achieving AGI. We could achieve it even with RNNs. But we need algorithmic improvements and better objective functions. More compute still makes a huge difference.
* We shouldn’t measure AI by human reasoning, because human reasoning is limited. AI will go way beyond human reasoning capabilities.
* We are way past “LLMs.” Gemini, Claude, and ChatGPT are complex multimodal systems, not just language models.
* Robotics will see significant improvements and much better generalization in the next 3–4 years, even without continual learning. Data diversity will contribute to near-term advances in robotics.

**[Watch the full conversation on the BuzzRobot YouTube channel](https://substack.com/redirect/b46fb400-ae86-4a2a-bfac-9b05d381366b?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)**

---

Another conversation I recently had was with **Tomaso Poggio**, a renowned **computational neuroscientist and professor at MIT**. Tomaso mentored **Demis Hassabis** (CEO of Google DeepMind) and **Christof Koch**, a neuroscientist who proposed Integrated Information Theory of consciousness, among other prominent scientists.

**Key moments from our conversation:**

* Gemini and ChatGPT are already past the Turing test for intelligence.
* In 2015, Demis Hassabis thought the path to AGI was 80% neuroscience and 20% engineering. In a more recent conversation between Tomaso and Demis, it’s 50/50—or the engineering part may be even higher.
* Current AI systems are good at simulating consciousness, but Tomaso believes today’s systems are not conscious.
* Tomaso is sympathetic to Manuel and Lenore Blum’s theory of consciousness: a “consciousness moment” is realizing something is important (for example, pain). If robots ever experience pain, Tomaso would consider them conscious creatures.

**[Watch the full conversation from my new show on AI consciousness](https://substack.com/redirect/6f51351a-0173-4754-92d9-e072e0f3310a?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)**

Check out previous talks by our guests on the [BuzzRobot YouTube channel](https://substack.com/redirect/f1d58298-fd62-4195-b0db-27581c2d577a?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ).  
  
[Join our Slack community](https://substack.com/redirect/199002c0-e188-491c-8d76-dbc87f3ef865?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) to connect with fellow developers, AI engineers, researchers, and practitioners.  
  
[Join me on X](https://substack.com/redirect/7c8e430a-4f7a-4b16-a080-ad4eae41a660?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ).

# [AINews] Moonshot Kimi K2.6: the world's leading Open Model refreshes to catch up to Opus 4.6 (ahead of DeepSeek v…

*Two days left before Early Bird ends for [AI Engineer World’s Fair](https://substack.com/redirect/b1974b8b-6cad-427e-8282-259cffdedf0c?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) this Summer in SF. This is will be THE BIG ONE of the year - lock in discounts up to $500 (refundable).*

---

[DeepSeek V4 rumors](https://substack.com/redirect/7e9566f8-65c3-49f2-8344-29a165f521a6?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) are back, and we learned our lesson not to get too excited, but in their deafening silence [since v3.2](https://substack.com/redirect/b4452054-dd98-40ee-93a7-e63d0d1b7ba1?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ), Moonshot has owned the crown of [leading Chinese open model lab for all of 2026 to date](https://substack.com/redirect/8615317b-411b-450f-a8ec-27b5a8c64f02?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ), and K2.6 refreshes the lead that [K2.5 established in January](https://substack.com/redirect/022d246f-0fc1-4488-842a-2a86edda6ab8?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ), with (presumably) more continued pre/posttraining (this time, details of how much more training were not disclosed). Comparing the numbers from the two launches 3 months apart demonstrates the staggering amount of progress:

[![](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!t76W!,w_1100,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Fba3bb8e1-94f7-4acd-a98b-e7d2ce0d577e_2886x1483.png)](https://substack.com/redirect/e3baa7fb-b92a-4906-b8e5-f78ca7431b13?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

Moonshot/Kimi continues to compete at a level far above “just being open source versions of Frontier models” (though it is one of [the three Chinese labs accused by Anthropic in Feb](https://substack.com/redirect/8ed440cb-d9e9-45b5-9ce3-dceed6014bef?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)) - they are taking on [Gemini 3.1](https://substack.com/redirect/941ac8eb-bbed-45ec-ae35-5b2ef0e1654c?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) in their home turf of frontend design, touting a 68.6% win+tie rate vs Gemini 3.1 Pro:

subject: Seedance, Kling and the Chinese AI Video Ecosystem
body:
# Seedance, Kling and the Chinese AI Video Ecosystem

It’s been a big week for Chinese AI video.

[ByteDance’s Seedance 2.0 and Kuaishou’s Kling 3.0](https://substack.com/redirect/1774ae85-87d5-4b14-877e-75fd3b6001a0?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) are going viral. Seedance probably takes the cake, being promoted for smoother motion, stronger scene coherence, and watermark-free downloads.

My favorite trend so far: people making videos of themselves cooking Lebron James.

[![](https://substackcdn.com/image/youtube/w_728,c_limit/l_youtube_play_qyqt8q,w_120/onDAcFF68NE)](https://substack.com/redirect/95de7ef2-520f-4f61-89e0-bdda2b64403f?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

On the other hand, the Cyberspace Administration (CAC) just [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/d5b46696-8f97-4f23-865e-a2154aa95551?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) it’s pre-Lunar New Year crackdown by removing more than 540k pieces of illicit AI content on Douyin, Wechat, and Weibo and taken action against over 13k accounts, making a statement that it’s stepping up enforcement of unlabeled or “garbage” AI-generated content.

China’s AI video ecosystem is moving at hyper-speed, while the CCP, typically the world’s most adept and overbearing content regulator, is scrambling to tighten control in real time. This is a bit puzzling, since China already has one of the most ambitious frameworks in the world for labeling and managing AI-generated content. **If the rules were put in place for a moment like this, why does it feel like they’re not working?**

Today:

* China’s new rules for labeling AI-generated content
* How those rules are being poorly enforced
* The domestic incentives behind this poor enforcement, including economic growth priorities
* The geopolitical incentives, including the use of AI to spread pro-China and anti-US propaganda

*Part two will give a broader industry overview of how Chinese models compare to Western ones, which companies are leading and targeting the Global South, and why video generation poses different training, open-source, and copyright implications for the Chinese ecosystem.*

[![](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!UEBE!,w_430,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F916beee3-380e-4614-a320-5a15cd681ee1_1536x1024.png)](https://substack.com/redirect/51e76017-4100-46e7-89c5-1a1d8d173876?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

China was the first country to introduce rules specifically for synthetic media—the [Deep Synthesis Provisions](https://substack.com/redirect/81e041a1-9cda-4e90-b5b0-55d7f7cd4f61?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) (互联网信息服务深度合成管理规定), which took effect in the dark ages of 2022.

Fast forward to March 2025: the Cyberspace Administration of China released the **[Measures for Labeling of AI-Generated Synthetic Content](https://substack.com/redirect/8e9dd73d-9450-4d7e-962d-6901c8db9f83?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)** (关于印发《人工智能生成合成内容标识办法》的通知). These rules require platforms to detect when content is confirmed, likely, or even just suspected to be AI-generated, and to attach both visible labels and embedded metadata by September 1st, 2025.

The accompanying national standard **[GB 45438-2025](https://substack.com/redirect/6d9c7bef-cd42-41fe-9ae0-58bb58a1c6ef?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)** spells out what those labels have to look and sound like:

* Images: visible text label covering at least 5% of the shortest side length
* Audio: spoken label at 120–160 wpm, or a Morse-code-style tone representing “AI”
* Video: clear labels shown at both the beginning and end of the clip
* Metadata: persistent, machine-readable tagging embedded in the file

China is essentially the only major country to enact a *pre

subject: Unitree's IPO
body:
# Unitree's IPO

In 2017, Hangzhou-based robotics firm Unitree 宇树科技 launched its first quadruped, Laikago. Laika was the name of the Soviet space dog onboard Sputnik 2, and the American English pronunciation of “go” is similar to that of the Chinese word for dogs, 狗 *gǒu*. Unitree’s battery-powered tribute to Laika wasn’t fuzzy, but walked on four feet and navigated through basic obstacles.

Unitree founder [Wang Xingxing](https://substack.com/redirect/11b32b32-f904-4258-8f60-e991656b6e6a?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) 王兴兴 has long held faith in the potential of robotic canines. Since 2020, when Unitree started gaining media attention, he has insisted in [multiple](https://substack.com/redirect/5f2c5a2c-478f-4938-9f1f-9832da495dbb?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) [interviews](https://substack.com/redirect/47d3b9f1-8ae8-4180-b61a-0d9b3bd68da8?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) that humans are drawn to four-legged creatures and will have a natural fondness for their artificial counterparts.

[![](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!rBoq!,w_1100,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F64d3cec2-87d5-4b93-a578-43c9d923ec01_796x451.png)](https://substack.com/redirect/98ecb78d-c033-4388-8b35-09efc03e2ce5?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

Wang Xingxing with a Laikago in 2017. (Source: [Bilibili](https://substack.com/redirect/520c62a4-b3f6-4f71-b270-b14616826576?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ))

Fast forward to 2026, and Unitree has just filed for a $610-million IPO on the Shanghai Stock Exchange. The company is a household name in China after its humanoid robots performed dances at the CCTV Spring Festival Gala for two consecutive years and counting. Through their IPO disclosures ([investor prospectus](https://substack.com/redirect/6590cfae-8c61-4d92-81d9-d78e1d715096?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) and [response letter](https://substack.com/redirect/7646fcc7-4c07-4334-bb95-70521e87c6c7?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) to the Shanghai Stock Exchange’s inquiries), we get some answers to important questions about the development of embodied AI.

* How is Unitree profitable?
* Where is diffusion happening inside China, aside from dancing on TV?
* Are Chinese robotics companies content to lead in hardware and applications, or do they also see themselves as pursuing some kind of generalized “frontier”?
* And finally, what does this all mean for US-China dynamics in robotics?

[![](https://substackcdn.com/image/youtube/w_728,c_limit/l_youtube_play_qyqt8q,w_120/mUmlv814aJo)](https://substack.com/redirect/22c4e469-c0c9-453a-96a1-9295a675e0e4?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

One of the most notable things about Unitree is the fact that it actually makes money. Unprofitability is a near-universal challenge because AI robotics, despite massive advances in the past few years, is still an early-stage technology. Mass adoption has not yet arrived; pathways out of bottlenecks like data are uncertain; and important safety [standards](https://substack.com/redirect/3ba714fa-eef7-4d5e-83e5-19a6c8c14555?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) have not caught up. Even shipping products consistently can be a challenge for some companies in the space, let alone manufacturing at scale and booking reliable customers.

This context is why observers have found Unitree’s ability to turn a profit remarkable. Not only has the company’s net profit been positive since 2024, but from 2024 to 2025, its net profit grew by 204.29%. A look at its growth, broken down by product category, reveals the most significant source of this revenue explosion: humanoids.

# [AINews] Claude Cowork Dispatch: Anthropic's Answer to OpenClaw

*Note: AIE Europe is ~sold out! Tickets and limited sponsorships for [AIE Miami](https://substack.com/redirect/44390dd9-5117-41cb-8c38-a420cb12e620?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) are next — as you can see from [online buzz](https://substack.com/redirect/0c154429-f3ed-4bdd-b498-3a6213e17821?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ), [speakers](https://substack.com/redirect/0d634119-e9ea-485b-8ad3-dc892d518cb9?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) are excited and prepping. We’ll be there!*

---

By total coincidence, today’s [main pod guest](https://substack.com/redirect/081098cf-80b8-4e08-98b0-d6a54c78e64d?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) also released today’s title story:

> **swyx**: Does remote control work for Claude Cowork yet? No. Right.
>
> **Felix**: Excellent question.
>
> **swyx**: Coming soon.

And today, [here it is](https://substack.com/redirect/33febd1b-6c62-4fd7-aa12-7009c54e7772?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ):

subject: Anthropic's Compute Advantage: Why Silicon Strategy is Becoming an AI Moat
body:
# Anthropic's Compute Advantage: Why Silicon Strategy is Becoming an AI Moat

Compute is not a commodity for frontier AI labs. It is a structural cost input that determines margin, throughput, and model iteration velocity at scale. The divergence in how Anthropic, OpenAI, and Microsoft have approached silicon procurement over the last 18 months is not just a supply chain story — it is a compounding strategic gap.

[![AWS, Anthropic Complete Project Rainier AI Cluster](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!poOF!,w_1100,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Fb5a36611-ba35-4595-ad62-6362cf5ad767_1280x720.jpeg "AWS, Anthropic Complete Project Rainier AI Cluster")](https://substack.com/redirect/4d41ea99-e6e2-4182-927a-d1f48f21f34e?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

###### Project Rainier, Anthropic and AWS

Anthropic has built what is today the most diversified and cost-efficient compute architecture among frontier AI labs. OpenAI remains almost entirely dependent on Nvidia. Microsoft’s internal chip program is years behind schedule. The structural implications favor Anthropic on unit economics and negotiating leverage as inference workloads scale. While Anthropic has had so much demand, it has struggled with up-time — its long-term strategy is the most fundamentally resilient.

[![](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!IyzI!,w_317,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F2c898b6e-c223-450e-872a-0667fabcd54f_317x234.png)](https://substack.com/redirect/f369bd04-339b-4351-be60-b14890e3f933?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

One important caveat up front: compute advantage amplifies model advantage; it does not replace it. If a competitor’s models are materially better, customers absorb the higher token cost. The argument here is not that Anthropic wins because of infrastructure. **The argument is that equivalent model quality delivered at 30–60% lower cost per token is a compounding advantage** — on margin, on training budget, and on the pace of iteration.

---

## The Structural Divide

Every frontier model company faces the same binding constraint: various estimates put Nvidia at ~90%+ of the discrete GPU market and a dominant share of AI training accelerators deployed in the field, and that pricing power is real. H100 on-demand list pricing at major hyperscalers (AWS, Azure, GCP) peaked at $7–$8/hour; even after the 2025 oversupply correction drove spot and commodity-broker rates to $1.50–$3.00/hour, the published on-demand rate at hyperscalers still runs $6–$9/hour. Committed and reserved pricing falls somewhere in between — typically $2–$5/hour depending on contract length and volume — but requires capital-intensive multi-year lockup.

The question is not whether you can afford Nvidia GPUs. At scale, the question is whether Nvidia is the only lever you can pull, and what that dependency costs you annually.

[![](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!alpJ!,w_400,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F47dddd82-7c1c-44b6-a0d8-10880f633053_400x316.png)](https://substack.com/redirect/bf77f687-96ea-46aa-aa56-7d16df87f1cd?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

[![](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!asw_!,w_468,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Ff53a17d0-8cc9-49ca-86dd-c597cb70e483_468x312.png)](https://substack.com/redirect/a498f6a6-8bd9-4c35-8952-529cbb2f1df7?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

There is a layer beneath the GPU pricing question that gets less attention: HBM supply. The real bottleneck in high-density AI clusters is not the accelerator die — it is High Bandwidth Memory,

# [AINews] Anthropic launches the MCP Apps open spec, in Claude.ai

> *AI News for 1/23/2026-1/26/2026. We checked 12 subreddits, **[544](https://substack.com/redirect/30f9d458-bf87-4bc5-a500-43542a1b8114?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)** [Twitters](https://substack.com/redirect/30f9d458-bf87-4bc5-a500-43542a1b8114?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) and **24** Discords (**206** channels, and **14285** messages) for you. Estimated reading time saved (at 200wpm): **1208 minutes**. **[Our new website](https://substack.com/redirect/b026cf7c-7022-4477-aadd-d91688c88389?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)** is now up with full metadata search and beautiful vibe coded presentation of all past issues.*
>
> *As a reminder, [AINews is now a section of Latent Space](https://substack.com/redirect/37f478a1-f45d-41c5-8ec0-90d8a1438446?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ). You can [opt in/out](https://substack.com/redirect/d33c697a-15bc-42bc-9ccb-b132a8ded92b?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) of email frequencies!*

3 months after OpenAI floated a trial balloon with [ChatGPT Apps and the Apps SDK at Dev Day 2025](https://substack.com/redirect/3cb8963a-5cf1-476b-996a-f6e29a87b557?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ), Anthropic has now officially absorbed [the independent MCP UI project](https://substack.com/redirect/2224f811-2226-4707-bad6-62b5b7f78aea?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) and, working with OpenAI, Block, VS Code, Antigravity, JetBrains, AWS, and others, has released both:

* [the MCP Apps spec](https://substack.com/redirect/1468ff65-548b-4865-bc6b-93713bebfe54?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)
* [official support in Claude.ai](https://substack.com/redirect/6a57d009-a4b3-4db6-ab18-251e8da4f662?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) - comparatively very well received but of course not as popular as [the Claude in Excel announcement](https://substack.com/redirect/d48d6025-640c-47c8-87e5-e6231c5f1cf8?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ).

It’s fair to say that ChatGPT Apps haven’t exactly taken the world by storm since announcement, but the overall need for a standard format for applications to return rich UI still cannot be denied.

Now that MCP Apps have been ratified by all the important players, this is the basis for a rich ecosystem of open source support and applications being able to interoperate, and perhaps one day solve the perpetual never ending pile of $20/month subscriptions piling up in your credit card bills.

As a reminder, we interviewed David Soria Parra and the rest of the AAIF, who previewed a bit of the thinking and design process behind MCP Apps here:

[![](https://substackcdn.com/image/youtube/w_728,c_limit/l_youtube_play_qyqt8q,w_120/z6XWYCM3Q8s)](https://substack.com/redirect/dfa46bb3-a121-46b0-aea4-d05919c1411d?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

---

**Agent Orchestration, RLMs, and “Clawdbot/Clawd” as a UX pattern**

* **NVIDIA ToolOrchestra + Orchestrator-8B**: NVIDIA’s ToolOrchestra frames agentic systems as a *small “conductor” model* that alternates reasoning with calls to tools and larger “expert” models (search, code execution, specialist LLMs, frontier generalists). The claim is that an **8B orchestrator** can reach *frontier-level outcomes* via delegation at materially lower cost, trained end-to-end with **scalable RL** using automatically synthesized tool-use environments and multi-turn tasks ([summary](https://substack.com/redirect/c3b76d0f-82a7-41c7-93e0-42e3e130d4bd?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ), [link](https://substack.com/redirect/1588dcb4-4f34-4931-821a-759a69b60c21?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQ

Available on ***[Youtube](https://substack.com/redirect/f41e5e13-5ba3-4d26-8219-0305d2c89bbb?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ), [Spotify](https://substack.com/redirect/5d0fe238-2a84-426e-b349-5d04bf804aa6?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) and [Apple Podcasts](https://substack.com/redirect/1a925b18-65a0-4bd5-8d7f-de87e86d9405?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)***

[Lee Robinson](https://substack.com/redirect/967b30ff-2a60-46fa-82c2-ef07bd4555b0?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) is the VP of Developer Education at [Cursor](https://substack.com/redirect/770f201e-5bb8-409b-9392-2da4c1d27332?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ), one of the fastest-growing AI developer tools (and companies) in the world. Before Cursor, he spent five years at [Vercel](https://substack.com/redirect/a5a22a8e-064c-4a5c-8c4b-5edd4a07f06d?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) helping define how modern developers learn and build on the web.

He’s also a husband and a dad to a young daughter, with a second daughter on the way. When I first invited Lee on the show, he had a five-month-old baby and felt like he was deep in the trenches of new parenthood. Nearly a year later, we finally sat down to talk about what that first year of fatherhood was really like.

In this episode, Lee shares how becoming a dad changed his perspective on work, ambition, empathy, and priorities. He talks about parenting while working inside hypergrowth startups, navigating family planning with an intense career, setting boundaries, sharing the load at home, and how Lee thinks about AI, education, and raising kids in a rapidly changing world. We discussed:

* **Becoming a dad inside hypergrowth startups:** What it was like navigating new parenthood while working at two of the fastest-growing companies in tech.
* **Questioning readiness for fatherhood:** How uncertainty, self-doubt, and honest conversations with his wife shaped the decision to start a family.
* **Miscarriage and pregnancy anxiety:** The emotional challenges that came before their first daughter and how it changed Lee’s perspective on control and fear.
* **Setting boundaries without losing ambition:** Why prioritizing health and family actually made Lee better at his job, not worse.
* **Sharing the load at home:** How Lee and his wife divide responsibilities, protect evening routines, and make remote work actually work for their family.
* **Raising kids in an AI-powered world:** Lee’s thoughts on education, curiosity, and why he wants his daughters to believe they can build and shape the future.

body:
# The Shape of the Thing

In October of 2023, I [wrote about](https://substack.com/redirect/b9136986-19c4-4222-88c0-de8860cd5f28?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) the “Shape of the Shadow of the Thing,” speculating on the Thing that AI might turn into in the coming years. I think we can see the Thing much more clearly now, and some of the consequences that come with it. As I have been discussing in recent posts, we have entered a new phase of AI. After ChatGPT was introduced, human-AI work took the form of what I called co-intelligence, where humans would prompt AI back-and-forth to get help on tasks. Starting in late 2025, we entered a new era thanks to AI agents like [Claude Code](https://substack.com/redirect/4069cec6-729f-4624-bce2-12bb86dca8d4?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ), OpenAI’s Codex, and OpenClaw. These are AI systems that you can just give work to, sometimes hours of human work, and get back reasonable and useful results in minutes. This is an era of [managing](https://substack.com/redirect/01545114-959c-4e3a-a4da-3f08c0858d81?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) AIs, rather than working with them.

This new approach to AI is the outcome of the rapid exponential improvement in AI abilities. That means you can’t understand where we are, and where we might be going, without understanding the increasing capability of AI.

Exponential improvements are hard to visualize, so rather than charts or graphs, I want to start with otters. If you have followed my writing on AI, you know about my [Otter Test](https://substack.com/redirect/d6113ad0-5283-41a3-bcb9-e91ff31cb797?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ), where I challenge various AI image models to show a picture of an “otter on a plane using wifi.” As you can see below, the progress from 2022 (the year ChatGPT launched) to 2025 was rapid and remarkable.

[![](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!3jtO!,w_529,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F3ac29474-e923-41ab-861a-0b1b5323d810_3146x2080.png)](https://substack.com/redirect/e499030b-65e7-427a-8269-bfb3fedaee2b?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

So, what has happened in the time since that April, 2025 image? With nearly perfect images, video has become the new frontier and has also seen exponential gains. To demonstrate, I gave the most advanced (and still unreleased in the US) AI video model from TikTok maker Bytedance, the prompt: *A documentary about how otters view Ethan Mollick's "Otter Test" which judges AIs by their ability to create images of otters sitting in planes*. This is the very first result — definitely turn on your sound:

[![](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!7KD3!,w_1100,h_618,c_fill,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/l_play_button_usfui2,w_144,e_colorize:0/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-video.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fvideo_upload%2Fpost%2F190587284%2Fa1ee3a83-e0f4-45f4-a182-ab0a4d872730%2Ftranscoded-01012.png)](https://substack.com/redirect/787a40b4-f5fe-41a8-bff5-41ac2a314319?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

Aside from a single pronunciation mistake, this is pretty perfect, down to the fact that the otters are animated to have human-like expressions. Of course, video models are cool, but they are not necessarily indicative of what useful agentic AI can do. So, what if we look at the benchmarks of AI ability, do we see the same exponential curve?

We certainly do in the most famous evaluation in AI today, the [METR Long Tasks graph](https://substack.com/redirect/f4f81f8e-f0ab-4d5a-9ae6-eff43c5709ff?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ). Вы замечали, сколько вокруг книг? Дома — полки с любимыми романами, потертые корешки детских сказок, которые перешли по наследству. В телефоне — библиотека на тысячи томов. Книги стали обыденностью, почти воздухом. Мы потребляем текст и редко задумываемся, откуда взялась эта привычная нам форма.

Оксфордский профессор Адам Смит однажды взял в руки фолиант XVII века и заметил на полях смазанный отпечаток пальца. След оставил печатник, который даже представить не мог, что через 400 лет кто-то увидит его прикосновение.

Так начинается новинка [«Книги и их создатели»](https://tn-sc.mckx.ru/c/UR4pAAAIaOgAwBSO/xiuEBw/-lnyPEx0V0d7ej8K/?u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.mann-ivanov-ferber.ru%2Fcatalog%2Fproduct%2Fthe-book-makers%2F%3Futm_source%3Dmindbox%26utm_medium%3Demail%26utm_campaign%3DAktivnayaBazaKnigiIIxSozdateli27-05-2026%23productType%3Dpaperbook%26amp%3BpromoCode%3DSOZDATELI)— рассказ об удивительных людях, чьи руки, ошибки и одержимость сделали книгу такой, какой мы ее знаем сегодня.

[СМОТРЕТЬ](https://tn-sc.mckx.ru/c/UR4pAAAIaOgAwBSO/xyuEBw/w3XJoipJrRYShSKx/?u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.mann-ivanov-ferber.ru%2Fcatalog%2Fproduct%2Fthe-book-makers%2F%3Futm_source%3Dmindbox%26utm_medium%3Demail%26utm_campaign%3DAktivnayaBazaKnigiIIxSozdateli27-05-2026%23productType%3Dpaperbook%26promoCode%3DSOZDATELI)

SOZDATELI

дает скидку до

50%

[на все книги МИФа](https://tn-sc.mckx.ru/c/UR4pAAAIaOgAwBSO/yCuEBw/gx6fG8IqecsFJd4U/?u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.mann-ivanov-ferber.ru%2Fcatalog%2Ftag%2Fnew%2F%3Futm_source%3Dmindbox%26utm_medium%3Demail%26utm_campaign%3DAktivnayaBazaKnigiIIxSozdateli27-05-2026%23books)

Действует до 23:59 (мск) воскресенья, 31 мая. *

## Библия из лоскутов

Англия, 1630-е годы. В уединенной общине Литл-Гиддинг две сестры, Мэри и Анна Коллетт, берут в руки ножи и ножницы. Перед ними — свеженапечатанные экземпляры Евангелия. Девушки начинают разрезать священный текст на кусочки. Предложения, отдельные слова, крохотные буквицы — все идет под лезвие. Вандализм? Кощунство? Ничуть.

На самом деле сестры создавали «Гармонии» — удивительные коллажи, в которых история жизни Христа собиралась из фрагментов сразу четырех канонических текстов. Они клеили, подгоняли, добавляли гравюры лучших европейских мастеров, и постепенно из разрозненных клочков рождалась новая цельность.

Получались книги невероятной красоты и веса — один том весил 23 килограмма и привел в восторг самого короля Карла I, который специально заезжал в Литл-Гиддинг, чтобы увидеть это чудо своими глазами. Эта работа — лучшее доказательство того, что в умелых руках книга становится не застывшей догмой, а живым материалом для творчества и веры.

## Шекспир, завернутый в Цицерона

В 1623 году выходит «Первое фолио» — сборник пьес Уильяма Шекспира. Сегодня за ним охотятся коллекционеры и аукционные дома, а тогда это была просто очередная книга, которую нужно переплести и поставить на полку. В Бодлианской библиотеке заказ отдали Уильяму Уайлдгузу — надежному мастеру «второго эшелона».

Уайлдгуз не читал Шекспира. Его зада

subject: On Doom Tabbing, Atrophy, and Addictive Technology
body:
# On Doom Tabbing, Atrophy, and Addictive Technology

My preferred use of A.I. for programming is Claude Code, planning mode sometimes, almost never auto accept edits. Go slowly, don’t put on the ring, hide from the eye of Sauron at the top of the tower. Stay vigilant against the doom tabbing. Exercise your will. Take breaks and hand-write some code. Go on a walk.

--

Using A.I. to write code feels very similar to the addictive relationship I have with my phone, and the self-control I try (and often fail) to have with managing its usage.

I have to try really hard to guard myself against it. I uninstall social media apps. I block instagram.com on my phone's browser.

My wife and I have been on this train for a while now. We've cancelled our Netflix account. Now we buy DVDs from the Goodwill. And sometimes we find them at the higher-tech booths at the antique malls. Our son likes sifting through them and picking something out for family movie night. We keep buying smaller and smaller TVs, hoping we'll want to use them less.

--

It seems that through the haziness of the hype, commercial usage of A.I. is really taking hold.

For a while, it was the dopamine-crazed vibe coders, hacking away in their free time, but not introducing this agentic workflow (or at least not publicly admitting) into their salaried work. But, and I have no stats or evidence to back this up, it seems that real usage is working into companies of all sizes.

More and more "sane" takes are coming out from trustworthy individuals, like [antirez](https://blog.slamdunk.software/r/a3042e05?m=5c42086f-1afa-4110-aebe-d27600431e6a). Just last month, Linus Torvalds, the last man standing in defense against machines, [has officially empoyed A.I. code generation](https://blog.slamdunk.software/r/e29ad3a5?m=5c42086f-1afa-4110-aebe-d27600431e6a).

These highly skilled, highly trusted technologists adopting these tools that sci-fi has warned us about, and that luddites have fought off since their inception, has stirred up a kind of existentialism amongst programmers.

![](https://blog.slamdunk.software/content/images/2026/02/Screenshot-2026-02-05-at-11.47.26---AM.png)

A comment on Linus Torvalds's monumental A.I. generated code commit

As companies small, medium, and large adopt sensible A.I. policies, I find myself returning to this [HackerNews comment](https://blog.slamdunk.software/r/f38f6343?m=5c42086f-1afa-4110-aebe-d27600431e6a):

> I worry about the "brain atrophy" part, as I've felt this too. And not just atrophy, but even moreso I think it's evolving into "complacency".  
>   
> Like there have been multiple times now where I wanted the code to look a certain way, but it kept pulling back to the way it wanted to do things. Like if I had stated certain design goals recently it would adhere to them, but after a few iterations it would forget again and go back to its original approach, or mix the two, or whatever. Eventually it was easier just to quit fighting it and let it do things the way it wanted.  
>   
> What I've seen is that after the initial dopamine rush of being able to do things that would have taken much longer manually, a few iterations of this kind of interaction has slowly led to a disillusionment of the whole project, as AI keeps pushing it in a direction I didn't want.  
>   
> I think this is especially true if you're trying to experiment with new approaches to things. LLMs are, by definition, biased by what was in their training data. You can shock them out of it momentarily, whish is awesome for a few rounds, but over time the gravitational pull of what's already in their latent space becomes inescapable. (I picture it as working like a giant Sierpinski triangle)  
>   
> I want to say the end result is very akin to doom scrolling. Doom tabbing? It's like, yeah I could be more creative with just a tad more effort, but the AI is already running and the bar to seeing what the AI will do next is so low, so....

--

Although it varies in degree,

# Reflexões sobre AI: Context Graphs, Unbundling e outras leituras

Encaminhou este email? [Inscreva-se aqui](https://substack..9T0H4f3gt0zK2NhpjJfCo2eMtaluNcMl_gpyHnyHGKg?) para receber mais.

*Olá, eu sou Guilherme, atuo como VC e apoio fundadores em early-stage. Na [DealflowBR](https://substack.com/redirect/e5b2c525-e446-4ae9-99a2-eb9ca34c130e?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) compartilho notas de campo, frameworks e curadoria para fundadores e investidores. O objetivo é separar o sinal do ruído na jornada de construção de startups. Todas as opiniões **são exclusivamente minhas**. Se quiser colaborar, me encontre no [LinkedIn](https://substack.com/redirect/7d2a9df3-7d2f-4d63-9b96-2557f35f1af1?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) ou responda a este e-mail.*

Se está conhecendo a newsletter pela primeira vez, se inscreva para não perder as próximas:

[Assine agora](https://substack..WZmVXVbcG2Pi2E0SX7M9rFWzLkYevGVBHZRVhd2wNTI?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=184679415)

---

Nessa virada de ano, após 5 anos, eu me despedi da Astella! Foi uma jornada muito rica e proveitosa, onde pude aprender e colaborar com pessoas de alto nível e empreendedores que admiro.

Agora, vou para uma nova. Há tempos tenho a vontade e interesse de criar e construir algo com minha autenticidade e alinhado com minhas crenças. Ainda não consigo descrever completamente o que vou fazer, mas uma coisa eu tenho certeza é que é estar ao lado de founders e criar valor por meio de tecnologia. Irei compartilhando alguns rastros e próximos passos por aqui.

Enquanto eu planejo e dou meus primeiros passos, **vou abrir alguns slots para [ajudar founders com desafios de fundraising e de criação de valor](https://substack.com/redirect/0bca25b2-3206-4a4a-a277-1615658aedc7?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) em Venture**. Meu intuito é apoiar founders para a aumentar a chance de sucesso e domínio da trilha de venture capital, trazendo a experiência de investidor e de board member de empresas investidas nos últimos 10 anos. Caso tenha interesse, clique aqui para saber mais e vamos conversar:

[Saber Mais](https://substack.com/redirect/0bca25b2-3206-4a4a-a277-1615658aedc7?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

…

Obrigado por ler até aqui.

Agora, vamos para a edição que conta com um compilado de reflexões e leituras das minhas férias. Foram algumas ideias, teses e atualizações sobre IA.

---

## Context Graphs

Esse é um assunto que surgiu da [turma da Foundation Capital](https://substack.com/redirect/c0b87081-1142-4eb5-b729-80f5f0999851?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) no final de dezembro, e rapidamente levantou discussões entre investidores e founders de IA, dada a clareza de uma tese e seu potencial. Na minha opinião, é uma perspectiva muito interessante sobre para onde está indo o desenvolvimento de IA e agentes para empresas.

So if you're using Shield and looking for somewhere to land, here's the analytics recap in 2pr.io:

1/ The basics done properly - impressions, reactions, comments, followers, engagement rate, posts - built on the official LinkedIn API, not a browser hook

2/ Best posting times heatmap - by day-of-week and hour, based on your own engagement, not a generic chart

3/ "What's working for you" - auto-insights like "Mondays land 1.5x harder" so you don't have to dig

4/ Bi-weekly coaching emails - we look at your last 14 days and send you what worked, what didn't, and what to try next, per post

5/ NEW - content mix: TOFU / MOFU / BOFU. Classic: top, middle, bottom of the funnel.

Then Alicia Teltz (whose community I'm part of) once dropped a rule on me: if you're under 10k followers, 70%+ should be TOFU.

Posts built for reach. Without volume up top, the rest of the funnel has nothing to convert.

# Robin Hanson on Cultural Evolution and Cultural Drift

[![Room recording - Jan 14, 2026.mp4](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!7uWw!,w_1138,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F95a6d973-f2ee-4f60-bc6f-2b23103a6ae3_320x180.gif)](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=866724&post_id=185052316&utm_source=podcast-email&play_audio=true&r=6wm0c&utm_campaign=email-play-on-substack&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjoxMTU5OTIxMiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTg1MDUyMzE2LCJpYXQiOjE3Njg4MzE0NDksImV4cCI6MTc3MTQyMzQ0OSwiaXNzIjoicHViLTg2NjcyNCIsInN1YiI6InBvc3QtcmVhY3Rpb24ifQ.ur6PGfKA9nUdeLCDbF7Q3KKX0BE2o93Tc6BscSnbbuM&utm_content=watch_now_gif)[![](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!JR-4!,w_26.046511627906977,c_scale,f_png,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack.com%2Ficon%2FPlayIcon%3Fv%3D4%26height%3D32%26fill%3D%2523ffffff%26stroke%3D%2523ffffff%26strokeWidth%3D2)Watch now](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=866724&post_id=185052316&utm_source=podcast-email&play_audio=true&r=6wm0c&utm_campaign=email-play-on-substack&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjoxMTU5OTIxMiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTg1MDUyMzE2LCJpYXQiOjE3Njg4MzE0NDksImV4cCI6MTc3MTQyMzQ0OSwiaXNzIjoicHViLTg2NjcyNCIsInN1YiI6InBvc3QtcmVhY3Rpb24ifQ.ur6PGfKA9nUdeLCDbF7Q3KKX0BE2o93Tc6BscSnbbuM&utm_content=watch_now_button)

Robin Hanson is Professor of Economics at George Mason University, the inventor of prediction markets, and the author of [Age of Em](https://substack.com/redirect/9ae32c48-8e26-4230-8074-3042b29e3128?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) and [The Elephant in the Brain](https://substack.com/redirect/6dcd9acd-8165-4dc6-9337-ebdaa86d0b87?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ). This episode is a deep dive into Hanson’s latest research topic, “cultural drift”, how we broke cultural evolution, why it threatens to end our civilization, and what we might do to fix it.

You can watch the interview here or listen to it on your favorite podcast app.  
  
The full transcript follows. It was transcribed in small chunks by Gemini 3.0 and spot checked but not fully verified by me.

---

**Ivan:** Today it’s my pleasure and honor to speak with Professor Robin Hanson, who is a professor of economics at George Mason University, the inventor of prediction markets—which are finally, after 30 years, having their day in the sun with the recent success of Polymarket and Kalshi. Robin is also the author of *The Age of Em*, about a really wild future involving human emulations, and the co-author with Kevin Simler of *The Elephant in the Brain*, which is about self-deception and the hidden motives in human behavior. Welcome to the show, Robin!

**Robin:** Great to be here. I am eager to talk about this subject. I’ve found that over the last three years, this is a topic that’s hard to get a lot of people to engage with, and I’m still struggling with understanding why. I’m eager for you to engage, but I’d be interested in your reflections or observations on what’s so hard about the subject.

**Ivan:** Maybe as a little bit more background to you first: as I mentioned, you’re a true polymath. Your interests over the years have ranged from prediction markets, futarchy—which is a new governance mechanism you’ve invented based on prediction markets—human emulations, signaling, grabby aliens, the sacred, the fertility crisis, and then finally cultural drift. I want to spend almost all our time today talking about cultural drift, but first I wanted to ask: how do you choose what to study next? This is a very eclectic collection of topics. Does it feel more unified to you?

## **Selecting Important and Neglected Problems**

# Import AI 442: Winners and losers in the AI economy; math proof automation; and industrialization of cyber espiona…

Welcome to Import AI, a newsletter about AI research. Import AI runs on arXiv and feedback from readers. If you’d like to support this, please subscribe.

[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..DqwQQ4bNYJmnKAOF8tw0CvNxa-7ay66i_OByLBlKfp4?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=185806002)

**The era of math proof automation has arrived:***…Numina-Lean-Agent shows how math will never be the same…*In the past few years, large-scale AI models have become good at coding and have also begun to generalize into other useful disciplines, especially those in math and science. Like with most aspects of AI development, the story has been one of increasing generalization and simplification of the systems as we shift away from highly specialized math models to just leveraging general-purpose foundation models and giving them the right tools to elicit their capabilities in a given domain.  
 The latest example of this is Numina-Lean-Agent, an AI system that uses standard, general foundation models to do mathematical reasoning. With this software, a team of mathematicians have solved all problems in the Putnam 2025 math competition - matching the performance of proprietary systems which use a lot more math-specific stuff - and have also used it to conduct some original math research, working with it to formalize the Brascamp-Lieb theorem.  
  
**What is Numina-Lean-Agent?** The software was built by a team of researchers from the Chinese Academy of Sciences, University of Liverpool, Xi’an Jiaotong-Liverpool University, Tongji University, University of Cambridge, Project Numina, Imperial College London, and the University of Edinburgh. The software is “a formal math reasoner based on a general coding agent”. It has a few key components:

* **Lean-LSP-MCP:** Software to allow AI agents to interact with the Lean theorem prover. “empowers models with the capability to deeply comprehend, analyze, and manipulate Lean projects”, and gives models a toolset for semantic awareness and interaction, code execution and strategy exploration, and theorem retrieval.
* **LeanDex**: Semantic retrieval of related theorems and definitions - basically, a search tool for theorems.
* **Informal Prover**: A system which uses Gemini models to generate informal solutions.
* **The most interesting tool of all: Discussion Partner:** A tool which “empowers Claude Code with the ability to ’seek assistance’ during Lean formalization: when encountering obstacles—such as proof bottlenecks, dilemmas in strategy selection, or ambiguities in intermediate lemmas—the primary model can proactively initiate discussions with other LLMs”.

**Discovering math together:** Along with the Putnam demonstration, the authors also used the software as an active partner in some math work, specifically formalizing Brascamp Lieb (I will not pretend to be able to explain what this means). “Over a period of less than two weeks of intermittent collaboration, the two human experts and the agent completed the formalization of more than 8,000 lines of Lean code. During this process, the agent autonomously introduced approximately 70 new definitions, lemmas, and theorems, illustrating its ability to actively extend the formal library and pa

# Should the US Buy from CXMT?

The “[RAMageddon](https://substack.com/redirect/d9cfef53-67c7-420f-9457-a2bd2916044f?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)” is here. Tears roll down gamers’ cheeks as AI ruins DDR5 prices. People are even [giving](https://substack.com/redirect/ff9e96a9-9122-491c-92af-04714d5ee0cc?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) RAM as wedding presents. Why is memory going to the moon, and what are the geopolitical implications?

[![](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!HR46!,w_1100,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F7348086e-f610-40dd-9e4f-d2377d8bfc24_2034x950.png)](https://substack.com/redirect/6b6199a0-c950-4df9-8100-d2d1ecb15112?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

Source: [PCPartPicker](https://substack.com/redirect/be1cec6f-695e-4894-bf87-d42b9e58bf91?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

The Big Three memory makers — SK Hynix, Samsung, and Micron — have dedicated increasing capacity to memory for AI, or HBM. High-bandwidth memory (HBM) is a product that stacks multiple DRAM dies for AI memory. The increased allocation toward high-margin HBM means that not enough capacity is reserved for memory chips for consumer products. Thus, products like phones, laptops, gaming consoles, routers, tractors, and hospital equipment may experience price increases and shortages, perhaps as late as 2028. Adding memory capacity is a years-long operation, and in the meantime, the people will suffer.

As a result, there is murmuring amongst everyone, from the [Pentagon](https://substack.com/redirect/599eeeac-6add-4c15-880e-d737cc8a6dd8?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) to [Apple](https://substack.com/redirect/fc01d31c-4612-4357-8801-4b919b807b6e?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) and to individual [gamers](https://substack.com/redirect/0c1f489c-198d-4a77-8ff3-04df9a91eca5?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ): perhaps the U.S. ought to turn to Chinese memory for consumer products. China’s leading DRAM company, CXMT, offers a compelling additional supply source. But the thought may scare conventional wisdom in D.C. Haven’t we been trying to decreasereliance on China? Why would we now open the floodgates on Chinese memory? In that case, perhaps the U.S. should instead ban or limit Chinese memory before the market creates unwanted dependencies.

Which is the right answer? **Should Chinese memory be welcomed or restricted?** This piece tries to answer the question by presenting both the case for and against Chinese memory. **Ultimately, after balancing the impacts on the economy and national security, this piece believes that the U.S. should welcome Chinese memory — for products destined to the Chinese market.** If customers can qualify CXMT for DRAM, then this would also lead to lower prices for American companies and consumers. The second-order benefits would be myriad, while the potential risks for market dependence and national security would be mitigated. Some risks, including assisting CXMT’s technological advances, are real but not sufficiently compelling.

## The Case for Chinese Memory

### Market Function

The most straightforward argument for allowing Chinese memory is to let the markets do what they will. Allowing Chinese DRAM from CXMT to compete with the Big Three will drive down prices for all. A naive calculation suggests that allowing CXMT unfettered access to American markets could increase global commodity DRAM supply by over 25%.¹

# The Trillion-Dollar Arbitrage: Blended Capital And The Future Of Deep Tech Investing

**Originally published in** ***[Forbes](https://substack.com/redirect/8bab79f6-be4c-4cbe-b704-29588279d024?j=eyJ1IjoiZnZlciJ9.8N73-dqQlrWLx3o5gPfyirClhk7-cxP_NqOwOQYAApk)*****[.](https://substack.com/redirect/8bab79f6-be4c-4cbe-b704-29588279d024?j=eyJ1IjoiZnZlciJ9.8N73-dqQlrWLx3o5gPfyirClhk7-cxP_NqOwOQYAApk)**

In the global push to build the next generation of breakthrough technologies—from orbital infrastructure to advanced physics—investors face a structural bottleneck. The [greatest hurdles](https://substack.com/redirect/28721820-c1fd-47d8-9aa0-1fe7bcb37e1e?j=eyJ1IjoiZnZlciJ9.8N73-dqQlrWLx3o5gPfyirClhk7-cxP_NqOwOQYAApk) in frontier science are no longer strictly technological; they are financial and structural. Traditional venture capital, driven by standard fund life cycles, is often [too impatient](https://substack.com/redirect/e9804703-f252-4766-8840-4dbf39564d73?j=eyJ1IjoiZnZlciJ9.8N73-dqQlrWLx3o5gPfyirClhk7-cxP_NqOwOQYAApk) to fund fundamental science during its most nascent stages. Conversely, [pure philanthropy](https://substack.com/redirect/6673e519-259d-4d7d-bb64-acd3ad8cb98a?j=eyJ1IjoiZnZlciJ9.8N73-dqQlrWLx3o5gPfyirClhk7-cxP_NqOwOQYAApk), while patient, lacks the commercial engine and aggressive scaling mechanisms required to build global, market-dominating enterprises.

[![](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!Zl5O!,w_1100,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Feb850f25-60e0-4f26-90d4-ab33d0e06839_1134x700.png)](https://substack.com/redirect/fa85669e-bd2b-41cd-8f6e-5d25cd3e7735?j=eyJ1IjoiZnZlciJ9.8N73-dqQlrWLx3o5gPfyirClhk7-cxP_NqOwOQYAApk)

The result is the infamous “[valley of death](https://substack.com/redirect/1fee4f9c-e8ba-4ee3-a098-d06fad7ce70c?j=eyJ1IjoiZnZlciJ9.8N73-dqQlrWLx3o5gPfyirClhk7-cxP_NqOwOQYAApk),” where promising deep tech innovations stall in the laboratory before they can reach the commercial market. For family offices, institutional allocators and wealth managers looking to enter the space economy and other frontier sectors, there is a powerful yet underutilized potential solution: blended capital.

### The Dual-Engine Approach To Frontier Tech

[Blended capital](https://substack.com/redirect/758d5430-dc03-41ab-95e6-e65642984c46?j=eyJ1IjoiZnZlciJ9.8N73-dqQlrWLx3o5gPfyirClhk7-cxP_NqOwOQYAApk) is the strategic sequencing of philanthropic grants and venture capital. In my dual roles leading a venture firm dedicated to deep tech infrastructure and advising global philanthropic initiatives, I have seen firsthand how this dual-engine approach functions. High-impact philanthropy can be deployed to intentionally de-risk fundamental research, acting as [catalytic capital](https://substack.com/redirect/e4933d4e-3bb4-484d-a641-101ed3dca2ea?j=eyJ1IjoiZnZlciJ9.8N73-dqQlrWLx3o5gPfyirClhk7-cxP_NqOwOQYAApk). It absorbs the initial, unquantifiable [risks](https://substack.com/redirect/51b7c0b6-41f9-45c2-957d-52bd61b6af44?j=eyJ1IjoiZnZlciJ9.8N73-dqQlrWLx3o5gPfyirClhk7-cxP_NqOwOQYAApk) associated with translating world-class research into a minimum viable product.

Once the primary technological risk is mitigated, traditional venture capital can step in. This handoff allows venture capital to do what it does best: aggressively scale the technology, build the operational team and capture the equity upside of a highly lucrative, global enterprise.

### Actionable Strategies For Wealth Managers And LPs

For single-family offices (SFOs) and institutional allocators looking to capture alpha at the ground floor of the [next trillion-dollar economy](https://substack.com/redirect/cd21c4fb-afde-4ef4-9228-d18c63fc24a1?j=eyJ1IjoiZnZlciJ9.8N73-dqQlrWLx3o5gPfyirClhk7-cxP_NqOwOQYAApk), blended capital offers a unique arbitrage opportunity. Here are three tactical ways to implement this strategy effectively:

#### 1. Strategically sequence your capital v

# Everyone has a launch plan until you ship it

[![](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!GUBc!,w_1100,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Fc0d3b087-f5ce-4c91-a870-5db80d8726e2_1832x734.png)](https://substack.com/redirect/5a378f37-1caa-424e-83e3-e9290c18af53?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

*The product you envision is not the product you ship - it’s the start*

*Hi, I’m Greg 👋! I write weekly product [essays](https://substack.com/redirect/f9f13e68-3b01-49a1-aa77-13c8736fd605?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ), including system “handshakes”, the expectations for workflow, and the jobs to be done for data. [What is Data Operations?](https://substack.com/redirect/ca362651-cc26-4de9-b1d8-5f7de4711912?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) was the first post in the series.*

This week’s toy: there’s a new emoji that came out —> a fight cloud! You might wonder how these get approved and created — read more [here](https://substack.com/redirect/0724c9c6-37aa-4656-bbf6-2fb5ff892ea9?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ).

Edition 301 of this newsletter is here - it’s May 4, 2026.

---

Thanks for reading! Let me know if there’s a topic you’d like me to cover.

---

## **The Big Idea**

*A short long-form essay about data things*

### ⚙️ Everyone has a launch plan until you ship it

[![](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!ehwB!,w_1100,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Fe9ad4d75-9b19-438b-a0a3-1e542c4ed343_1832x734.png "")](https://substack.com/redirect/5a378f37-1caa-424e-83e3-e9290c18af53?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

“Everyone has a plan until they get punched in the mouth” - Mike Tyson, 1987

People have been paraphrasing Mike Tyson’s boxing quote about about business plans since he said it. If you think it doesn’t apply in software, you need to go through a launch to see it happen.

Take side projects. They sound like a great idea when you talk to Claude (*“You’re so insightful!”*). If you’re building a product on nights and weekends, you have a plan. You can describe what it does in two sentences. You wrote the landing page, and you are the core user. You believe all of it.

Then a stranger uses the build.

The punch is the moment your code is in someone else’s hands and they’re using it differently than you described it. Every assumption you made about what they’d see, click, expect, miss, or never find is being tested in parallel by people who don’t share your context. The plan was a closed system. The build is an open one.

As a product person, here’s the shift to notice. Before you ship, your bottleneck is the plan. Refining the pitch, the funnel, the deck is where you put your effort.

After you ship, your bottleneck is the loop between the build and the people using it. Most builders never make that transition. **They keep optimizing the plan when the plan is no longer the constraint.**

### What the plan can’t see

From inside the plan, here’s what feels solved:

- **The user’s intent.** You imagined what they need. You wrote copy in their voice — or what you imagine their voice to be.

- **The funnel.** You labeled the steps. You wrote the CTA, the email, the next email.

- **The pitch.** You can describe the product cleanly. Two sentences. Maybe three.

- **The build.** It works on your machine. You’ve used it. It does what it should.

The plan compiles cleanly because there is exactly one judge in the room and they already agree with the verdict. The product feels obvious because you’re the only one who has ever been confused by it, and that was four months ago. You haven’t seen what it look like when you’re not in the room and someone tries it out for the first time.

[![Beton's new user interface](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!soQn!,w_1100,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F9185dc49-1e2b-42e6-9317-d3a521f78905_2895x1563.png "Beton's new user interface")](https://substack.com/redirect/d23f8391-e678-432d-afc9-ee98ba35ac1d?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

the release is [live in production](https://substack.com/redirect/53b820b7-1c11-49aa-86df-76e0df148bf5?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ). let’s go through it, but first – subscribe if someone has forwarded this to you:

## **neo-brutalist design inside the app**

the landing pages have had the thick borders, flat colors, and monospace type for a while. now the entire app matches

app now looks like landings — not a generic dashboard with a branded landing page

## **firecrawl integration**

we saw LLMs work better when given a dedicated scraping/crawling tool

it seems more context about upgraded or closed/won customers will help Beton’s agent choose signals better

so, you can now connect a Firecrawl instance

bring your own API key or turn on cloud spend – already in [Settings](https://substack.com/redirect/cd267608-750d-4592-8ad6-2c3ab8f84b59?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

once we teach our agent to use it, it will

* look at what a company actually says on their website
* cross-reference it with their product usage patterns
* give you a fuller picture of intent

**try before you buy**

we’re doing a lot of Posthog these days and we saw how confused the early users were

the old flow was:

```
sign up
→ stare at empty screens
→ (not) figure out which API keys go where
→ give up
```

we’ve changed the app to solve this. the new flow is:

```
land on inspector 
→ see everything working with demo data
→ decide if you want it in couple of clicks
```

every screen works in demo mode. no login, no credit card, no PostHog key required

there’s a `“Demo Mode”` badge so you know you’re looking at fake data, and a login button on every screen for when you’re ready

after you sign up, setup is a 6-step wizard:

1. PostHog connection,
2. Attio API connection,
3. field mapping – so you set up how your Beton generated deals will look like,
4. your domain,
5. billing,
6. Firecrawl – optional step, will be more useful in 1-2 weeks

> if you’re self-hosting with `AUTH_BYPASS=true` in env vars, you can skip any step

I tried as much as I could to drop some UX sugar. these were small things that saved me a lot of back-and-forth in other SaaS I use

let us know if UI is still confusing

## **your AI agent can talk to inspector**

inspector now ships with a full MCP server — 18 tools covering accounts, signals, CRM mappings, billing, everything

1. go to `/settings/mcp`
2. copy the JSON config
3. paste it to your agent – and it’s connected

the MCP settings page has four tabs:

* **Setup & Installation** — server URL, auth config, one-click install snippets for popular agents
* **Methods Reference** — all 18 tools documented, split into read-only and write/mutate, grouped by category with parameter docs
* **Connected Sessions** — see which agents are currently connected, with a detail sheet for each session
* **Request Logs** — filterable, paginated log of every MCP request hitting your instance

## **new navigation**

the sidebar went from a flat list to a proper nested structure:

```
Home

Signals

Identities

▾ Memory

    Exploration Logs

    Website Assumptions

    DB Structure

▾ Settings

    Integrations

    Billin

subject: Sari Azout: Mother, Where Do You Stand, Third Chair, Crazy, Nirvana
body:
# Sari Azout: Mother, Where Do You Stand, Third Chair, Crazy, Nirvana

Welcome to a new issue of *Words That Matter*! Each week, we invite a guest curator to share the reading that matters most to them.

Our curator today is Sari Azout ([@sariazout](https://substack.com/redirect/3fb474cc-d4b2-4775-9720-696ce62326ad?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)). Sari is the founder of [Sublime](https://substack.com/redirect/fc01c42b-7864-4760-82c7-19c45f253a09?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ), an inspiration tool used by thousands of thinkers and creatives to collect ideas. cultivate taste, and make work that feels distinctly human in an age of AI. She also writes a [Substack newsletter](https://substack.com/redirect/8e3dd13a-834b-4041-b191-81757cc7b41b?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ), where she reaches 70,000+ readers with musings on tech, culture, creativity, and building thoughtfully in these strange times.

Please enjoy these works and words that have mattered to Sari!

## Sari’s Picks

### [Pre, Mid, Post-Training Way of Life](https://substack.com/redirect/e8857ccf-a69b-44d4-9377-c3607039461f?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

[Tina He](https://open.substack.com/users/47506-tina-he?utm_source=mentions)

I had to read this essay several times to understand it, but wow, Tina is such a gifted writer. She manages to do several things in this piece: explain how modern AI training works, use that as a metaphor for different kinds of human minds, and turn it into a spiritual question about what we’re optimizing our lives for. Highly recommend.

---

### [Mother](https://substack.com/redirect/2c98f869-e8b8-49d9-b8d1-09c8ea682755?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

[Mills Baker](https://open.substack.com/users/11256580-mills-baker?utm_source=mentions)

A personal reflection on the author’s relationship with his mother that brought me to tears, This quote stopped me in my tracks: “It is easier to survive a category five hurricane than it is to get through an ordinary Wednesday afternoon. My mother was defeated by Wednesdays.”

---

### [I’ve had several disagreements with friends about where you stand on things. Where do you…stand?](https://substack.com/redirect/c29a64b0-48e8-45d4-8883-599b2e17498f?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

Nick Cave

Filed under things I wish I wrote. *I am comfortable with doubt and am constitutionally resistant to moral certainty, herd mentality and dogma. I am disturbed on a fundamental level by the self-serving, toddler politics of some of my counterparts – I do not believe that silence is violence, complicity, or a lack of courage, but rather that silence is often the preferred option when one does not know what they are talking about, or is doubtful, or conflicted – which, for me, is most of the time.*

---

### [Backseat software](https://substack.com/redirect/e7b7ed64-97ef-4357-a710-43d599bfe56c?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

Mike Swanson  
  
If you’re trying to build something good today, this essay is a powerful defense on intuition, and touches on what happens when optimization eats vision and experimentation becomes the primary decision making tool. Reminds me of The Score by C. Thi Nguyen, the best things are impossible to fully represent in a graph.

---

### [The Third Chair](https://substack.com/redirect/7ed1b668-fed1-4244-ab35-42c695adfab1?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

[Henrik Karlsson](https://open.substack.com/users/850764-henrik-karlsson?utm_source=mentions)

Just trust me. It’s short (400 words) and will give you goosebumps.

---

### [Face it: You’re a crazy person](https://substack.com/redirect/158257e7-6485-4673-b80b-89d47b5eda7a?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

[Adam Mastroianni](https://open.sub
