subject: Ed Luttwak on Military Revolutions
body:
# Ed Luttwak on Military Revolutions

This show’s guest is the legendary strategist Edward Luttwak — the Machiavelli of Maryland. He’s consulted for presidents, prime ministers, and secretaries of defense, and authored magnificent books on [Byzantine history](https://substack.com/redirect/d059d882-ed5d-46dc-a9b1-74c4fd5fc68c?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ), a [guide](https://substack.com/redirect/d6d5ef7a-0a7f-4453-be78-2a9b25468a6e?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) to planning a successful coup, and [an opus](https://substack.com/redirect/0d0cb848-fd84-4e20-8861-95a953fc0a8c?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) on the logic of strategy and the rise of China. He raises cows, too.

### This is the full-length transcript of our conversation.

**Our conversation today covers…**

* **Luttwak’s childhood and formative encounters with war, including an early fascination with the mafia in Sicily,**
* **Technological step-changes in warfare,**
* **Books that shaped Luttwak’s view of war, from Clausewitz to the Iliad,**
* **The costs of “removing war from Europe” post-1945,**
* **China’s strategic missteps,**
* **The psychology of deterrence, including what kind of Middle East policy would actually deter Iran,**
* **The strengths of democracies vs. autocracies.**

Listen now on [your favorite podcast app](https://substack.com/redirect/5e6bf5c3-271d-4e28-bdf1-dc391344d378?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ). Note, we recorded this in the summer of 2024.

[![](https://substackcdn.com/image/youtube/w_728,c_limit/l_youtube_play_qyqt8q,w_120/qYxFHyh_NVs)](https://substack.com/redirect/5eafccd9-35b2-40d9-869e-a39a3b2929be?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

**Jordan Schneider:** Let’s talk about your approach to history. Because in reading, ingesting a lot of you over the past month or so, you have this very unique approach, which is almost like an everything-everywhere-all-at-once view, both when you’re doing your Byzantine stuff as well as the more contemporary work looking at the modern world, which is not something you see very often.

I guess there aren’t a lot of historians who are fluent in as many eras and regions as you are, or even try to synthesize as much and draw from as many different examples in trying to pull out threads and a thesis. Maybe, how did you come to this approach? What inspired it? How did you develop this style?

**Edward Luttwak:** Well, if I were to answer honestly, you would realize that I invented none of it. I can’t claim credit for having initiated anyway. Accidents of life brought me successfully into contact with people of all kinds.

It started with the fact that I was born in Transylvania, in Banat, actually, Northwest Romania, which is an area that was within Romania, but was not Romanian. The population included Serbs, there were Hungarians, there were Germans, Catholics, German Protestants, there were Hungarian Calvinists, Hungarian Catholics, Jews of different kinds, and of course, Romanians as well. It was the only truly multinational part of Europe, the only multinational place in the whole of Europe.

Down the main boulevard where the house where I was born was, there was the Serbian Cathedral, the Orthodox Jesuit, Romanians, the Hungarian Catholic Church, the Calvinist Church, the German Lutheran and so on. There were schools for all these languages, and people conversed in them. It was truly multinational. The Romanian government had a very light hand because it was by far the most prosperous part of Romania, which generated all the high tax revenues, and they didn’t want to mess with it. They didn’t fly to Romania — There was no brutal imposition of Romanian uniformity, of anything of the sort.

Stop using your old, broken chart of accounts! It’s much easier to run accounting if you have a good foundation. It will also make finance (and the CFO’s) job much easier. Grab my chart of accounts template and how I track departments below 👇

[OnlyCFO Chart of Accounts Template](https://substack.com/redirect/d3912c7f-24ce-43ac-841d-f7819dc7c605?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

---

I am going to start publishing regular newsletters on current tech, finance, and other stuff that I find interesting.

It’s a way to catch people up on the latest stuff for those who aren’t terminally online like I am. And share my thoughts on the events.

### 1. Capital One Acquires Brex for $5.15B

Everyone has been talking about Capital One acquiring Brex. The opinions from social media were mixed:

* “A $5B acquisition is a top 0.001% outcome!”

But many people tried to push a more negative angle:

* “Brex lost to the competition.”
* “Brex **only** sold for $5B. They were valued at $12.3B in 2021.”
* “Brex employees didn’t make any money.”

My favorite meme in response to all this is below… Lots of opinions from folks who have never built anything near Brex’s scale. $5B valuation is amazing and Brex built an incredible business. Full stop.

[![](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!wHkG!,w_1100,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F944ebd8b-2157-4283-997d-4de62b8c5797_621x417.png)](https://substack.com/redirect/ad8cd280-fd8a-4c80-9687-6d735cceedd7?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

Yes, Brex is down from the crazy valuation days of 2021. But so is almost every other software/fintech company. Cloud stocks are down ~52% on average from their peak.

[![](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!hJxV!,w_1100,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F0c1c0841-0e30-43b0-8339-7a503b1620ab_1596x1038.png)](https://substack.com/redirect/59e35ee4-1933-4a97-941c-507cbea09f08?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

> **So was $5.15B a good price for Brex?**

Yes. What we currently know is that Brex crossed $700M in ARR at the end of August last year, was growing ~45%, and had 50% gross margins. Assuming some decent growth duration, Brex is probably at ~$800M ARR today and will probably end 2026 at $1.1B-$1.

# SaaSpocalypse: We Have Met the Enemy and He is Us

The day has come. Software is officially dead (again)! At least this is what the public markets seem to have decided. In the last twelve months, public SaaS is down an average of 32%¹, and the drawdown has already surpassed the COVID selloff.

[![](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!80PX!,w_1100,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Fdbe78859-ac73-4943-a756-8975f798a4ff_993x622.png)](https://substack.com/redirect/c517967e-c5f3-4862-8988-8ad10fd08b59?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

[![](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!KCU2!,w_40,c_scale,f_png,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack.com%2Ficon%2FLucideCheck%3Fv%3D4%26height%3D40%26fill%3Dtransparent%26stroke%3D%25235a7afe%26strokeWidth%3D3.6)Subscribed](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9ibG9nLnNhYXNob2xpYy5jb20vYWNjb3VudCIsInAiOjE4OTI1MDk4NiwicyI6MjU1MjMxNCwiZiI6dHJ1ZSwidSI6MTE1OTkyMTIsImlhdCI6MTc3MjQ1MzcyOCwiZXhwIjoyMDg4MDI5NzI4LCJpc3MiOiJwdWItMCIsInN1YiI6ImxpbmstcmVkaXJlY3QifQ.pet1A2nbJhEOwSITqXPsrdh5HZyh3KJP64nKiwix1YQ?)

SaaS has, for two decades, been the holy grail of tech investing from Silicon Valley to Wall Street. The business model combines economics that let it compound over time: high growth, high margins, an asset-light structure with high switching costs and recurring revenues, leading to great retention that enabled tech companies to grow faster than other publicly traded industries.

Cloud software has consistently grown 30% annually for 20 years, giving comfort and the benefit of the doubt for investors to “pay up” for a growth that would always arrive. High growth was rewarded in a world where growth in the real economy was harder to find and interest rates were 0. This led SaaS to trade at high revenue multiples (without needing to worry about profitability, yet), with the median SaaS trading from 5–10x ARR and top-quartile growth names at 20–30x.

[![](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!h4Np!,w_1100,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Fbeeca5e9-cba1-4f67-be84-b8ca17dfd188_988x610.png)](https://substack.com/redirect/3049ff5e-024e-4f37-9f0f-817c8c9de426?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

However, it seems like AI is challenging every single one of the assumptions that made SaaS the hottest business model in town.

As seed investors not directly exposed to the public downturn, we believe the AI-driven reshuffle is good news. The largest names in software a decade from now will probably look very different from today, opening the doors for newcomers to build the next wave of winners.

Let’s break down what is driving the market pessimism.

#### **Public market growth is not what it used to be**

Markets want high growth. However, growth rates for public SaaS have been declining for years. At the same time, AI is the new highest-growth opportunity available, and we have seen many AI companies beating record revenues in short periods of time, whether in the LLM space (Anthropic growing from $0 to $10B ARR in 3 years), the application layer (Cursor from $0 to $1B in 2 years), or infra (with NVIDIA’s revenue quadrupling to $130B since 2022).

Markets are searching for growth and public SaaS isn’t fully delivering it (which also helps explain why more dollars are flowing to private markets).

[![](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!H98p!,w_1100,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F87cdef9c-5a0c-48e3-b015-74efa56b41c8_900x577.png)](https://substack.com/redirect/0103fa6a-6fc2-4833-b029-7217671e802c?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

I've joined Inflection as CMO.

This comes from last week's news that [Inflection acquired Keyplay](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/ss/c/u001.jGY3i_l4dDwQlqT7xK9Awow5hCfkWIjgDT9fAUTEiSideG0UKA56VoypV0t3Z0DGlQnhQxljbxT3fNLj50dv99GSdRI17ieFOkD3UlDcu4IEXcUFPIdALAO-kMJYIRJNuvHuze_05ecnUVFvV0OYvoJUnUdiZdSVFmaY5QEpP5x0SZMIOEbCGX_cIiCLtWdUrOWDhXVz3t50-49FR91QeZ4o2M8gGQZNIfcIRJkq1jeBKSVulWw76Ih8WQT3pbFkWqp_8WIZLwmRzoQyQiv3VdXY7PtYui0j66PiyvU_lhh9n99OdoRvYo5vf8IJyn4B1Qa8DIxZBjeHneqcqc9RgSvUSkijp-exbb6x9nXR7RE/4pu/O8TrxeNKSAGFNt5z8RnCdg/h6/h001.g4dkohzItDE1nVLlp_TlPmxKUaG5vkSObERmNjTTm_E).

My reasons for joining are typical: Team, market opportunity, mission that fits my strengths, exciting role, right timing. And for bonus points, I'm working for a CEO I've known and trusted for 15 years.

But my onboarding has been different.

Over the last 5 months I've become "extremely AI pilled" ([as Ramp calls it](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/ss/c/u001.jGY3i_l4dDwQlqT7xK9Awow5hCfkWIjgDT9fAUTEiSideG0UKA56VoypV0t3Z0DG9U4rLB2piHEmm2ArkSOvsUvc3Wy3B248ejbldOHYu8tka7UDxX5poLy8HN80HLKBtcONtcKLFfP-v61yD_Ehh6R3sEn1DwrW4fEx2duWMoywAO7dw3sokhZjUhOLGGUi68nNv2jQLBFf9CGIi70SXaya5Fz1PN9qDcTxIywQOLDnv605eSRTYuQh32IDm_sjTLh7QOSxf11i92Ufynb9pkFgk73rRn4MHIkFGbNXCzluDCv7qFovhrsN7XpyDU6OghBpGoTk8WOEv8EXBzvcXUa83Jr-9O8lAbzrvUKZZ-g/4pu/O8TrxeNKSAGFNt5z8RnCdg/h7/h001.HYc2RUn2b2YY6qsJocU56nldYKgCxQMw6vj3EYI0wV0)).

So as I enter this new role, I have to go full AI-pilled and be an "AI-Native CMO."

I honestly don't know yet.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/d5b80876-3cc1-4687-b681-7a995a7175d4/image.png?t=1776307561)

But I think the only way to figure it out is to take a pretty extreme posture and avoid doing a lot of the traditional onboarding steps. So that's what I did. I figure this will bring a lot of learnings that I can share here along the way.

To start, here's what I'm doing for a "full AI" CMO onboarding.

**1.) No traditional 30/60/90.** First week, I set up a Claude Code personal operating system. Local files organized into three buckets: context, work, system. Every project starts in Claude Code. Every decision and output flows back into context. The system gets smarter every day because the context compounds. Here's my simple architecture, not 1,000 folders:

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/75441eea-ef52-4d69-86a1-78daa944d3d6/claude_setup.png?t=1776306592)

**2.) Built Claude skills WHILE I work.** I didn’t just sit down and write skills. I started doing work, then build skills around that work. After a couple weeks I had skills to analyze pipeline data from Salesforce, search customer call transcripts for key positioning nuggets, surface content ideas, draft campaigns, and track team activity. I have a /morning skill that gives me a daily feed of what's happening internally (Slack, Notion, Calendar) and externally (calls, SFDC, LinkedIn). It's like a personalized briefing that knows my priorities.

**3.) Launched a centralized "GTM Context" resource for the team.** I helped create a central knowledge base that everyone's agents can draw from. Positioning docs, customer stories, call transcripts, ICP definitions, win-loss analysis. Everyone is still digesting [the OpenAI vs Anthropic launches](https://substack.com/redirect/681b9ad0-22cd-400c-9afa-ab1c5a45a013?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ), and the truth will out.

We’ll use this occasion to step back a bit and present **seemingly unrelated items**:

* In [A sane but extremely bull case on Clawdbot / OpenClaw](https://substack.com/redirect/4cbe951f-bc15-4af5-a807-ee49c138b01c?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ), the author uses **the same agent** **as a central cron job** to remind himself of promises, accumulate information for calendar invites, prepare for the next day, summarize high volume group chats, set complex price alerts, take fridge freezer inventory, maintain a grocery list, booking restaurants and dentists, filling out a form and have Sam Altman’s “[magic autocompleting todolist](https://substack.com/redirect/be85a209-a3e8-48c7-a38a-5612e36078c7?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)”.
* The distribution hack that Moltbook uncovered is the installation process [immediately installs a HEARTBEAT.md](https://substack.com/redirect/827d590f-7fa4-4cb3-bb6b-c834df1ccfc1?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) that **takes advantage of OpenClaw’s built in [heartbeating](https://substack.com/redirect/c15e5de0-6845-476e-977a-25e9deb4354d?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)** to power the motive force of the agents filling up Moltbook

  [![](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!tEjU!,w_413,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Ffab4e4b2-27ab-428b-bb81-c7c21e8e68d7_1746x998.png)](https://substack.com/redirect/2b957c26-7bb8-4b58-8e78-22ecb1e325b6?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

# Space 2055: What Will the Space Industry Look Like in 30 Years?

**Issue 165. Subscribers: 84 842**

[![The Future of Human Space Exploration](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!u2k-!,w_1100,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F7fee73fa-5bb4-4814-a722-ed66fc3d94aa_1500x914.jpeg "The Future of Human Space Exploration")](https://substack.com/redirect/e68606fb-83e7-4149-924d-65efcb4115a2?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

NASA artist concept of future crews living and working on the Moon. Source: NASA/Davidson

The morning of March 20, 2055. At an altitude of 400 kilometers above Earth, a new crew takes over a commercial space station. In a few hours, a cargo spacecraft carrying equipment for a new pharmaceutical experiment will dock. Producing certain drugs in microgravity has proven to be far more efficient than on Earth.

At the same time, a suborbital passenger flight crosses the Atlantic. The journey from New York to Singapore takes less than an hour. These flights are still expensive, but for business and time-critical logistics, they have already become a routine part of the global economy.

A bit farther from Earth, in lunar orbit, a transport spacecraft is preparing to dock with the Artemis orbital station. From there, cargo is delivered to the lunar surface, where a permanent base is already in operation. Water is extracted from polar craters and processed into rocket fuel for interplanetary missions.

Back on Earth, billions of people don’t even realize how much of their daily infrastructure depends on space. Internet access in remote regions, weather forecasting, transportation, and agricultural management—all of this is enabled by vast satellite constellations.

Sounds inspiring, doesn’t it?

*At Space Ambition, we decided to look ahead and imagine what the future of the space industry might look like.*

*This article is a forward-looking exploration rather than a precise forecast. It reflects our perspective on how the space industry might evolve over the next 30 years, based on current trends, emerging technologies, and a fair amount of informed speculation.*

> Speaking of the future, we’re curious to know whether space-data centers will be cost-effective. At Space Ambition, we’ve conducted an extensive study with calculations on this topic. ***Write to us if you want to receive it!***  
>   
> We provide consultancy services for stakeholders in the SpaceTech and DeepTech sectors. Whether you’re an investor, corporation, aerospace agency, accelerator, incubator, ecosystem builder, startup founder, or planning to launch a SpaceTech or DeepTech business, we can help.
>
> Contact us at **denis@spaceambition.org**—we’d be happy to assist. Good luck with your future endeavors!

Of course, the scenario described above is an optimistic one.

For it to become a reality, several key factors need to align:

* a dramatic drop in the cost of space launches;
* the emergence of sustainable space markets (less dependent on governments);
* a solution to the problem of space debris;
* and the absence of a large-scale geopolitical confrontation in space.

[![Ben Cooper Rocket Launch Photography - SpaceX, ULA, NASA photos](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!-vpQ!,w_1100,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Fd14c9b54-5cba-4359-be4f-535363edaab6_1050x700.jpeg "Ben Cooper Rocket Launch Photography - SpaceX, ULA, NASA photos")](https://substack.com/redirect/74f4fc60-206d-4996-b04b-9e13a668337f?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

Falcon 9 launches Starlink 10-57. Source: launchphotography.com

This is the fundamental factor. Without it, none of the other scenarios are possible. Today, the cost of launching one kilogram of payload into orbit is [around $7,000.](https://substack.com/redirect/a535b692-c75a-

> [![Attio Raises $23.5 Million Series A to Usher in a New Era of ...](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!2XL6!,w_437,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Fd46e3db9-6382-4ae6-8982-66431cbd5ea2_1200x456.jpeg "Attio Raises $23.5 Million Series A to Usher in a New Era of ...")](https://substack.com/redirect/be41b95a-1239-4a97-baeb-01ddda412b8b?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)
>
> Your CRM is only as good as the data in it. **[Attio](https://substack.com/redirect/c072deb8-3697-443e-aee3-75494769fb91?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)** is the AI CRM that keeps itself accurate. Then automate what used to be manual: workflows that update records, route leads, and keep your pipeline clean without chasing reps. No more data silos. No more cleanup projects. **[Try for free →](https://substack.com/redirect/c072deb8-3697-443e-aee3-75494769fb91?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)**

---

Revenue teams run a lot of meetings. Most of them are too long, cover too much ground, or fail to generate decisions. But two specific meetings matter more than any other in the RevOps cadence: the weekly business review and the quarterly business review. They share an acronym structure and a common purpose of keeping revenue on track, but that’s about where the similarity ends. Conflating them is one of the most consistent operational mistakes I see in growth-stage companies, and it costs teams real decision-making quality.

Getting both meetings right requires understanding what each one is actually trying to accomplish, who should be in the room, and what the outputs look like when done well. This article walks through the mechanics of each, where teams tend to go wrong, and how to structure both so they actually generate signal rather than status theater.

---

The WBR is an operational meeting. Its job is to keep the revenue machine running from week to week. It surfaces what’s working, what’s not, and what needs to be fixed before it becomes a bigger problem. The QBR is a strategic meeting. Its job is to explain what happened over the prior quarter, why it happened, and what the team is doing differently as a result.

These are fundamentally different cognitive tasks.

The WBR asks: are we on track, and if not, what do we do right now?

The QBR asks: what patterns emerged, what do they tell us, and how do we change course?

[Robert Whitney](https://substack.com/redirect/e51aff27-739e-454b-8d6d-882129be0701?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) is the Co-Founder and CTO of [Hapiko](https://substack.com/redirect/acd98675-605f-4215-a8d7-0560a92c598b?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ), the company that invented [Stickerbox](https://substack.com/redirect/c06ad3a4-b88b-4757-9537-b61d39920bfd?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ), an AI powered product helping kids create and play in more imaginative ways. He’s also a co-parent to a four-and-a-half-year-old son in New York City. In this conversation, Robert shares how fatherhood changed the way he approaches work, decision-making, discipline, and presence. We also talk about co-parenting as a founder, his shift away from a hard-partying New York lifestyle, the parenting principles he’s developed, and why he believes most AI products are failing kids. We discussed:

* **Why parenting is the ultimate life experience:** How becoming a dad made Robert more grounded and less reactive.
* **Co-parenting while building a startup:** What it looks like to split time as a founder and a parent, and how Robert thinks about being fully present in each mode.
* **Leaving behind a hard-partying New York lifestyle:** Why Robert made a major life change years before becoming a dad, and how sobriety reshaped his priorities, energy, and sense of self.
* **How loss changed his perspective on fatherhood:** What losing his mom shortly after becoming a parent taught him about time and presence.
* **What most AI products get wrong for kids:** Why Robert believes kids need safer, simpler, more thoughtful tools.
* **How Stickerbox started with his son:** The rainy-day moment that turned into a company built around play and creativity.

# There is no pivot

[![The Real Meaning Of 'There Is No Spoon' In The Matrix, Explained](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!EW5N!,w_1100,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Faf7c1152-a139-4397-a504-0892d6b4d846_1600x901.jpeg "The Real Meaning Of 'There Is No Spoon' In The Matrix, Explained")](https://substack.com/redirect/d883f445-703b-4461-b579-2ab4ed878db3?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

[Only try to realize the truth.](https://substack.com/redirect/2e87eaac-98c7-4d0a-afc7-4818e831f3a6?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

Here is what “pivot” means:

1. While sitting around in a conference room with a couple coworkers, you have an idea for a startup. “Man,” you say about some internal tool you built at your company, “Nighthawk / Stuffie / Vulcan / Hacky Sack / Shake ‘n Bake is really good. What if we made a business out of it?”
2. Or, while reading about some other huge startup—Uber, Stripe, whatever—you come up with some way to apply their solution to another problem. “Man,” you say while looking at how big the company is, “What if there was [Uber for drugs](https://substack.com/redirect/e6771b8d-bdb4-4f91-ac03-429a2bfba34d?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)? Or [eBay for drugs](https://substack.com/redirect/66586923-63ee-4b21-91f3-65c23ac57d81?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)? Or [Stripe for drugs](https://substack.com/redirect/ddc3408e-ce2d-40b4-a94d-f6c8ebaf007b?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)? Or [iPhone for drugs](https://substack.com/redirect/d157f91c-85ca-47d5-9969-dbe32c64f7a5?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)?”
3. You research it. You talk to potential customers. You pitch it to investors. You convince a few of them that it is a good idea, and they give you money, to use technology to sell drugs.¹
4. You hire engineers and designers, and spend months—years?—building a delightful product. You hire marketers, and spend months—years?—carefully crafting a striking brand. You recruit “design partners;” you cultivate a “community.” You launch your product with great panache.
5. At some point months—years?—later, you eventually realize that your idea was, in fact, not a good idea. Despite your comprehensive research and delightful product and striking brand and great panache, nobody is using your app.
6. This is a problem! You spent a bunch of money building something nobody wanted! You hired a bunch of experts to solve a problem that didn’t need to be solved! You filled your phone with drug dealers, and you are not doing any drug deals.
7. And so, you do it—compassionately, in front of the entire company, and later, resolutely, on LinkedIn: *We must Pivot.* You say you still care deeply about your original mission, but the timing is off. The product was too early; the market was not ready. You are grateful for your passionate customers—their support has meant everything—but the landscape has shifted, and we must evolve too. We cannot be afraid of hard choices. Today is a tough day, but it is the beginning of a new chapter. In building our app, we have built several exciting technologies. We have made many useful [community connections](https://substack.com/redirect/1db24934-b0ad-4870-9446-432e996c01d6?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ). We have been researching a new idea; we have been talking to potential customers; we are sure that this one is a good idea. We have made this decision deliberately, and now we will do it forcefully. [Gradually and then suddenly.](https://substack.com/redirect/8deda05a-d709-4a47-a7a7-7052e38ec97e?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) We are excited for what’s next.

# How do you make a chart?

[![name a chart!](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!oyV3!,w_1100,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F3fa30641-fc68-4e7b-b4ff-a434c760c142_836x460.jpeg "name a chart!")](https://substack.com/redirect/4623cb67-f719-4e88-9a3c-fe920176fdab?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

[Draw a chart! Draw any chart!](https://substack.com/redirect/b88a975e-566a-49b9-9c15-e9f33a01a775?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

How do you make a chart, in the age of artificial intelligence? You have many choices:

1. Give an Excel file to an image model like [Nano Banana](https://substack.com/redirect/d41f8138-98b2-4240-9154-7c00b6564631?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) or [ChatGPT Images](https://substack.com/redirect/26c43aa1-b2c1-42ca-af25-b16dd79450ad?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ), and tell it to make a picture. Have it read your data, squint at some imagined piece of paper in its head, and draw a bar chart, of the Charlotte Hornets 2025-26 season, in a nostalgic 1990s aesthetic.¹
2. Make your chart directly in Excel. Use [AI in Excel™](https://substack.com/redirect/1e6216be-73aa-48e6-aeb2-dfb1600919ae?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ), powered by Microsoft 365™ Copilot™. Or, other models [can use computers now](https://substack.com/redirect/bda0ebad-f85c-419c-8d7d-cf5fcfcbb7c4?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ); tell them to take over your computer, open Excel, click “New chart,” and flip through all of Excel’s menus and dropdowns.²
3. Ask an AI to use a simple charting library to create the chart with code. There are so many: Matplotlib, Plotly, Seaborn, ggplot2, Bokeh, Highcharts, Observable, Vega, Vega-Lite, Apache ECharts, Google Charts, Fusioncharts, ZingChart, Chart.js, [I could do this forever](https://substack.com/redirect/dc082a82-eeb7-4d8f-b8af-dce469e172db?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ). The robots will create your chart with a few simple configurations, like defining which fields go on which axis, and let the charting library handle the exact details.³
4. Ask it to make the chart using a low-level charting framework like [d3](https://substack.com/redirect/b03b872d-20ca-468a-957d-6af7f3b97271?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ), “the JavaScript library for bespoke data visualization.” In other charting libraries, there are concepts like “bar charts” and “legends.” In d3, there are concepts like “rectangles” and “text.” It’s a collection of visual Lego bricks: Most of the bricks are shaped like things that might be useful for making charts, but you can make anything with the bricks.⁴
5. Make the chart using native Javascript. Javascript is the language that people use to create *any* website—YouTube, Wordle, the [homepage for the original](https://substack.com/redirect/10f94c49-b75d-4899-9db0-40125c6e4a11?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) *[Space Jam](https://substack.com/redirect/10f94c49-b75d-4899-9db0-40125c6e4a11?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)*. If Highcharts lets you draw charts, and d3 lets you draw shapes, Javascript lets you draw *anything*.⁵
6. Make the chart in [C](https://substack.com/redirect/008a39d0-8b26-466b-a403-83828be017a4?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ). C is a general-purpose programming language for creating programs and operating systems. If AI can do anything, why should it use Excel, a browser, or even Windows? That is generic software. It should create a program designed for making exactly the right chart. It should design an *operating system* designed for making exactly the right chart.⁶
7. Make the chart in a bespoke programming language. De

subject: Considerations on Cultural Drift
body:
# Considerations on Cultural Drift

> *Like most humans ever, I love my culture. Its food, clothes, festivals, songs, stories, news, monuments, inspirational speeches, all of it. Deeply. They bring tears to my eyes, and comfort to my soul. I want to assume, as have most humans ever, that the mere fact that my culture exists suggests that it will probably do well by me. And the fact that it seems especially envied and celebrated raises my hopes further.*
>
> *[…]*
>
> *It turns out that, since I’ve learned about [cultural drift](https://substack.com/redirect/8f721b7b-7e79-498a-9480-947572f476f0?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ), I do in fact see my culture as broken. But for some reason I can’t or won’t look away. And I struggle to express to you just how very betrayed and adrift I feel as a result. I’ve lost my trust in something that I’ve implicitly and deeply loved and trusted. I will stay loyal to my loved ones, but I can’t stay loyal to my culture, including its key norms and status markers.*
>
> ~ Robin Hanson, [Betrayed by Culture](https://substack.com/redirect/78141d93-f4e2-4008-842e-f61b9fba1932?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

Robin Hanson is one of the few true polymaths of our age, his interests over the years including prediction markets, futarchy, human emulations, the importance of signalling to human psychology, grabby aliens, the sacred, and the fertility crisis. For as long as I’ve followed his work he’s been extremely optimistic about the future - from signing up for cryonics to pooh-poohing the risks from artificial intelligence, Hanson’s always seen the future as vast and bright - if not necessarily for biological humans then for our AI or emulated descendants.

But a few years ago, his writing took on a darker tone, and has been getting bleaker and more desperate ever since. He believes he’s identified a flaw in our civilization, a flaw that’s likely to prove fatal to it. [And virtually nobody’s listening](https://substack.com/redirect/14a5b199-96a9-4d11-aef1-a9d3f6cc2345?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ).

So I decided to investigate, by [interviewing Hanson](https://substack.com/redirect/4db38568-8cc8-4aa4-8419-a7ecff963252?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) and then by writing up my own thoughts on the topic after some hours of reading. If you want Hanson’s full views I recommend listening to the interview or reading the transcript; in the rest of this article I’ll summarize his argument and outline some of my remaining questions and confusions.

A core prerequisite for engaging with these ideas is the *Cultural Intelligence Hypothesis*, popularized in my intellectual circles by Joe Henrich’s book [The Secret of Our Success](https://substack.com/redirect/06598fe0-dbe8-4fb7-959f-b676e17c88df?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ). Henrich argues that the primary driver of humanity’ spectacular success vis-a-vis other species was not our individual intelligence, but rather our innate capacity for creating and maintaining *cultural* knowledge - i.e, copying the behavior of nearby humans, especially humans with high prestige.

[![](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!C7ph!,w_1100,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Fb40ea8d5-b579-420f-8b77-59ba89b389a7_600x406.png)](https://substack.com/redirect/af55fcd2-0908-4956-b0a1-1a6f0d14f821?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

Tomasello et al (2005) showing humans’ proficiency at cultural transmission

It is cultural evolution - the slow accumulation of adaptive behavioral patterns over millenia - that is responsible for modern civilization and everything we call “progress”. And, according to Hanson, this key driver of human progress [is now broken:](https://substack.com/redirect/42dd65a8-68e8-4805-

### Andrew Jones | Creator of Data Contracts, Principal Engineer & Author

[![](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!ASP9!,w_1100,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Fcb7d17eb-2d23-4b01-9e4c-7e598d1e9215_1600x900.png)](https://substack.com/redirect/35e7aace-08e8-46fd-9592-72cc4355505c?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

[Andrew Jones](https://substack.com/redirect/ef0d9e55-83f1-4fed-a83b-54f33459ade0?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) is a Principal Engineer and Author, specialising in modern data architecture and platform design. He is widely recognised as the **creator of data contracts**, an approach introduced in 2021 that redefines how organisations manage data quality, ownership, and governance by treating data as a product with explicit, enforceable interfaces. He is also part of the LinkedIn *[Top Voices](https://substack.com/redirect/4e92e0e1-1a93-4d49-941e-f788d5fe2067?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)* recognition, an invitation-only group of experts across the professional world.

Andrew has spent over a decade building large-scale data platforms, including leading foundational data platform initiatives at *GoCardless*, where he pioneered the implementation of data contracts to enable reliable, revenue-generating data products. He currently serves as a Principal Data Engineer at *Springer Nature*.

In 2024, he authored a [definitive book on data contracts](https://substack.com/redirect/8ab0fab5-50e3-454b-8319-da82f468f873?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ), consolidating years of practical experience into a widely adopted industry reference. Beyond his technical work, Andrew is an active contributor to the data community, a member of *Google Developer Experts*, and part of the technical steering committee for *Bitol*, helping shape open standards for data contracts and data products. We’re honoured to feature his insights on [Modern Data 101](https://substack.com/redirect/cd1b13d1-3b42-403c-85ea-af4d0d1ac832?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ).

> *We actively collaborate with data experts to bring the best resources to a [20,000+ strong community](https://substack.com/redirect/5262a2bf-2551-4b73-8eee-a11d63f7e851?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) of data leaders and practitioners. If you have something to share, reach out!  
> 🫴🏻 Share your ideas and work: [community@moderndata101.com](https://substack.com/redirect/67053a7b-638a-4ddd-a81c-9ff9be10990a?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)*

###### *\*Note: Opinions expressed in contributions are not our own and are only curated by us for broader access and discussion. All submissions are vetted for quality & relevance. We keep it information-first and do not support any promotions, paid or otherwise!*

---

### Let’s Dive In

Traditional data platforms are a mix of disparate datasets with different attributes, different capabilities, and different levels of governance, each created and managed through complex custom workflows.

For data consumers, this results in data that is **difficult to use.** Every time someone wants to consume a dataset, they need to gather all the context required to do so, from scratch, often by tracking down and asking the right individual in the organisation. This increases the cost of using data, reducing its applicability.

Then, once they have found enough context to make use of the data, consumers often find it **does not work well with other datasets**.

There are no standard naming conventions, and no common keys to join on. If they want to join this data, they will have to create complex pipelines to do so first.

On the other side, data producers find **publishing data is expensive and time-consuming

# Nomads vs locals in Mexico City

**Welcome to Borderless, Plumia’s weekly newsletter for global citizens, third culture kids, and digital nomads.** We handpick the best links to help you navigate the quirks of working online and living across borders.

---

[![](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!PHxX!,w_1100,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F59ea6a6b-eb5e-4f7d-a084-a7fd0998487a_1456x1048.png)](https://substack.com/redirect/9d469df6-9a60-4db4-bd02-dc335ca3f453?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

###### **NOMAD HUBS**

**🇲🇽 [Mexico City’s nomad boom meets organised backlash](https://substack.com/redirect/bd1717e7-b800-460c-a265-aee6337b87e2?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)**

Tenants and activists tie rent hikes to dollar-earning newcomers, while others blame city hall and a long-strained housing market. The debate is now playing out in protests, not just posts.

**Padraig Moran** *for* **CBC**

[![](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!aY8v!,w_1100,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Fd965be84-69e8-4a53-bb19-df2dba8d1c53_1200x7.png)](https://substack.com/redirect/1c9f0304-1ba5-4650-afc7-ce7e817ac6c6?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

###### **NOMAD VISAS**

**🇧🇹 [Bhutan rolls out a blockchain-powered nomad visa](https://substack.com/redirect/56236e74-4eb0-482d-ba22-43d7d559fcec?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)**

Visa processing meets crypto infrastructure, wrapped in a kingdom better known for “Gross National Happiness” than Web3 pilots. One-off experiment, or viable template for how smaller states plug into nomad capital?

**Jamie Redman** *for* **Bitcoin.com**

[![](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!aY8v!,w_1100,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Fd965be84-69e8-4a53-bb19-df2dba8d1c53_1200x7.png)](https://substack.com/redirect/1c9f0304-1ba5-4650-afc7-ce7e817ac6c6?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

###### **TRAVEL TIPS**

**🍃 [Dolma, the stuffed dish the world fell in love with](https://substack.com/redirect/b072bb97-ab44-409b-8d81-595f71efeccb?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)**

One dish, many homelands. From the eastern Mediterranean through the Caucasus and beyond, dolma travels with people—folded, rolled, and claimed along the way. A recipe that maps migration better than most passports.

**Soumya Gayatri** *for* **BBC Travel**

[![](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!aY8v!,w_1100,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Fd965be84-69e8-4a53-bb19-df2dba8d1c53_1200x7.png)](https://substack.com/redirect/1c9f0304-1ba5-4650-afc7-ce7e817ac6c6?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

# We're Are All Wall Dancers Now

*A new show with [afra](https://open.substack.com/users/2227115-afra?utm_source=mentions), [coulda been at the club](https://open.substack.com/pub/couldabeenattheclub?utm_source=mentions), and [Lauren Teixeira](https://open.substack.com/users/39570-lauren-teixeira?utm_source=mentions)* *just dropped on the podcast feed about CHINAMAXXING. [Have a listen here](https://substack.com/redirect/055cb803-edc3-4482-afc0-b10e0a85d890?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ).*

*Also below we’re featuring an interview Afra did with Yi-Ling Liu.*

---

*[GovAI](https://substack.com/redirect/0e5b6b46-3590-4fdc-805e-bd0eeb590617?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) was founded ten years ago on the belief that AI would end up transforming our world. Ten years later, the organization is at the forefront of trying to help decision-makers in government and industry navigate the transition to advanced AI.*

*GovAI is now hiring for its next cohort of [Research Scholars](https://substack.com/redirect/8b9be4b5-4e9a-46bc-a221-5a92b1fdecb3?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) and [Research Fellows](https://substack.com/redirect/06754094-5550-44df-af32-01596fb43d96?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ). Scholars are one-year positions that provide an intellectual home for ambitious researchers and policy professionals looking to advance their careers or transition into AI policy. Fellows are longer-term positions for experienced researchers with an established track-record looking for a place that supports their most impactful work.*

*Both roles offer significant freedom to pursue policy research, advise decision-makers, or launch new initiatives.*

*Applications close **15 February 2026.** Learn more and apply at [https://www.governance.ai/opportunities](https://substack.com/redirect/714d116b-ae44-4431-b0e2-145f21825fbf?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ).*

---

If there’s any book I’ve been anticipating for years, it would be this one: *[The Wall Dancers: Searching for Freedom and Connection on the Chinese Internet](https://substack.com/redirect/be19e956-b117-4e7c-b32e-a3b1cecbdf05?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)*, written by [Yi-Ling Liu](https://substack.com/redirect/f19f60f6-75cc-493a-be36-a2781de16f0a?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ), a friend and a role model. She writes about a Chinese entrepreneur who runs the world’s [largest gay dating app](https://substack.com/redirect/0d665234-da33-49c7-a26d-c4e9ab4ef9e1?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) and once shook hands with Premier Li Keqiang (now deceased). She writes about how [GitHub became an information haven](https://substack.com/redirect/366b2d23-4cae-4fa5-97c4-1e91fecde4cc?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) during COVID censorship. She writes about [the hyper-growth and malaise of TikTok](https://substack.com/redirect/856a2439-a51a-4820-8d51-4dfd1fe4b7a8?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ): a global company both blessed by realized ambition and cursed by geopolitics.

If there’s a converging theme, Yi-Ling’s work always returns to technology and political participation in China, a place long portrayed by familiar discourse as internet’s aberration; *Chinese internet is a prison, not the free, equal, and luminous internet we were promised!* Yet by 2026, that discourse had aged poorly. The internet and tech world we now inhabit increasingly resembles China’s in its inner logic and ultimate purpose, not the other way around. Look at how US-owned [TikTok censors content](https://substack.com/redirect/299b173c-ceb0-4767-abcd-8e3d2363716e?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ), a familiar playbook for Chinese internet natives.

# VEON Announces 2026 AGM and Board Nominees 

![VEON LOGO FINAL 2022](https://hs-9256877.f.hubspotemail.net/hub/9256877/hubfs/VEON%20LOGO%20FINAL%202022.png?width=388&upscale=true&name=VEON%20LOGO%20FINAL%202022.png)

**VEON Announces 2026 AGM and Board Nominees**

**Dubai and New York, March 31, 2026** – VEON Ltd. (Nasdaq: VEON), a global digital operator, (“VEON” or the “Company”), today announced that its Board of Directors (the “Board”) has set the date for the Company’s 2026 Annual General Meeting of Shareholders (the “AGM”) for May 11, 2026 at 12:00 Gulf Standard Time. The record date for the AGM has been set for March 31, 2026.

The Board and its Nomination Committee have recommended VEON’s seven current Board members for re-election at the AGM. The recommended nominees are Augie K Fabela II, Andrei Gusev, Sir Brandon Lewis, Duncan Perry, the 70th U.S. Secretary of State Michael R. Pompeo, Michiel Soeting, and the Company’s Chief Executive Officer Kaan Terzioglu.

Commenting on the slate of director nominees, the **Chairman of the Board and its Nomination Committee Augie K Fabela II stated:** "VEON’s performance in 2025 underscores that our strategy is delivering, and this momentum supports continuity at the Board level. This progress was exemplified by the August 2025 NASDAQ listing of Kyivstar, highlighting the intrinsic value of our business. Building on this, our digital operator strategy continues to drive strong results, with digital revenues growing 84.1% year-over-year to 20.1% of Group revenue in 4Q25. In parallel, with our SpaceX global partnership, we are advancing the integration of terrestrial and satellite networks. Together, these efforts—along with continued expansion in digital, financial services, and AI inclusion—reflect disciplined execution."

In addition to the election of Board members, the AGM agenda includes the re-appointment of UHY LLP as external auditor of the financial statements for the Company for the financial year ended December 31, 2026, as well as the receipt by shareholders of the report of the Company’s auditor and the audited financial statements of the Company for the financial year ended December 31, 2025. 

Further details on the Company’s AGM, including information on the re-appointment of UHY LLP, summary biographies on the slate of nominees seeking election to the Board, voting and procedural matters, will be made available through an official notice distributed by VEON to its registered shareholders of record prior to the meeting.

**About VEON**

VEON is a digital operator that provides connectivity and digital services over 150 million connectivity and more than 205 million digital users. Operating across five countries that are home to more than 6% of the world’s population, VEON is transforming lives through technology-driven services that empower individuals and drive economic growth. VEON is listed on NASDAQ. subject: Wait... What actually is the Claude logo?
body:
# Wait... What actually is the Claude logo?

I've been looking at the Claude logo since May 2023. Anthropic [had just released a 100k context window](https://blog.slamdunk.software/r/f379a87b?m=5c42086f-1afa-4110-aebe-d27600431e6a). A lot of people didn't really believe that Anthropic could actually provide us with a context window that large, or that the model could use it effectively.

And just this week, this message has popped up in Claude Code:

> ↑ Opus now defaults to 1M context · 5x more room, same pricing

But, that's not what this post is about. What I want to talk about is: *what the hell is the Claude logo*?

I don't know why, but I've never really thought about it. It looks sort of like a sketch. Hand-drawn. It does convey the feeling that Claude is perhaps more DIY than the buttoned-up OpenAI logo.

Is it an asterisk? `*`? If so, what would that mean?

Is it a sun, a star-burst of sorts?

## The Elephant in the Room

I will admit, this is not where my mind first went, but it's hard to deny—is it a butthole?

[Why do AI company logos look like buttholes?

A humorous exploration of the uncanny resemblance between AI company logos and human anatomy. Discover why circular, gr…

![](https://blog.slamdunk.software/content/images/icon/apple-touch-icon.png)
VelvetShark](https://blog.slamdunk.software/r/ffea18bf?m=5c42086f-1afa-4110-aebe-d27600431e6a)

As you can see in the video loop above, it, sort of, pulsates. That does not seem like the behavior of an asterick.

Maybe it's just an abstract logo that they chose for little reason, used the company branding color, and called it a day?

## Claude Shannon

Claude, after all, is named after Claude Shannon.

Donald Knuth mentioned this recently in his [Claude Cycles essay](https://blog.slamdunk.software/r/5aa76787?m=5c42086f-1afa-4110-aebe-d27600431e6a).

> I think Claude Shannon’s spirit is probably proud to know that his name is now being associated with such advances. Hats off to Claude!

Is there some connection between the Cluade logo and Claude Shannon? Something I'm not picking up?

## Abstract, Amorphous Blob

This is my best guess as to what Anthropic is going for. I think they're trying to somehow represent the unrepresentable nature of AI, and this Claude logo is like an amoeba. An amorphous blob. It's squishy. It's evolving and adapting every day.

There's no way it's a butthole, right?

[![Comment](https://static.ghost.org/v5.0.0/images/comment-mobile.png)

# Булгакову 135. Перечитать и влюбиться заново

[![](https://email-images.mindbox.ru/1ca2061c-10d5-4234-82bc-922f99c7de8e/7.png)](https://tn-sc.mckx.ru/c/LtooAAAIoJYAwOqu/Yx54Bw/eNlK6T8kWgjR3rsx/?u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.mann-ivanov-ferber.ru%2F%3Futm_source%3Dmindbox%26utm_medium%3Demail%26utm_campaign%3DAktivnayaBazaDrBulgakova15-05-2026)  

[НОВИНКИ](https://tn-sc.mckx.ru/c/LtooAAAIoJYAwOqu/ZB54Bw/TwlcNZIxw1TjSwZN/?u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.mann-ivanov-ferber.ru%2Fcatalog%2Ftag%2Fnew%2F%3Futm_source%3Dmindbox%26utm_medium%3Demail%26utm_campaign%3DAktivnayaBazaDrBulgakova15-05-2026%23books)

  [![](https://email-images.mindbox.ru/6e04741e-9e4c-49ae-a716-415df9973e05/1.jpeg)](https://tn-sc.mckx.ru/c/LtooAAAIoJYAwOqu/ZR54Bw/t-V3Fslvxw-myHjm/?u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.mann-ivanov-ferber.ru%2Fcatalog%2Ftag%2Fnew%2F%3Futm_source%3Dmindbox%26utm_medium%3Demail%26utm_campaign%3DAktivnayaBazaDrBulgakova15-05-2026)

Однажды Михаил Булгаков собрал альбом газетных вырезок с отзывами на свои пьесы. 298 рецензий — отрицательные. Три — положительные. Он аккуратно подклеил и те и другие. И продолжил писать — потому что иначе просто не умел.

Наверное, за это мы его и любим. А еще за кота Бегемота, за нехорошую квартиру, за то, как смеялся над тем, над чем смеяться было страшно. И, конечно, за «Мастера и Маргариту», которую в пятнадцать читаешь про магию, а сейчас — про себя.

![](https://email-images.mindbox.ru/2deca75b-9cbb-4bda-864d-0392b7a891a8/4.png)

В день рождения писателя признаемся в любви ему — и всей классической литературе. По промокоду **BEGEMOT26**  вас ждет **скидка 50%** на книги из разделов [Классика](https://tn-sc.mckx.ru/c/LtooAAAIoJYAwOqu/Zh54Bw/QPSMg3IyRtlVejFN/?u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.mann-ivanov-ferber.ru%2Fcatalog%2Ftag%2Fnew%2F%3Fshelf%3D2%26shelf%3D4%26shelf%3D5%26utm_source%3Dmindbox%26utm_medium%3Demail%26utm_campaign%3DAktivnayaBazaDrBulgakova15-05-2026) и [Классика Young Adult](https://tn-sc.mckx.ru/c/LtooAAAIoJYAwOqu/Zx54Bw/wmMrrr2QIn4dAQIe/?u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.mann-ivanov-ferber.ru%2Fcatalog%2Ftag%2Fnew%2F%3Fshelf%3D2%26shelf%3D4%26shelf%3D5%26utm_source%3Dmindbox%26utm_medium%3Demail%26utm_campaign%3DAktivnayaBazaDrBulgakova15-05-2026). Приходите за тем, что однажды уже читали. Или за тем, до чего только собираетесь добраться.

А пока — спиритическая разминка. Сможете угадать, какие книги Булгакова скрываются за описаниями?

![](https://email-images.mindbox.ru/0edb3a71-308d-48f6-9577-657a5febd4b7/6.png)[![](https://email-images.mindbox.ru/a1b9c354-d763-495b-bf6e-732126f74a58/3.jpeg)](https://tn-sc.mckx.ru/c/LtooAAAIoJYAwOqu/aB54Bw/EDTIk2HqLIJb4fdm/?u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.mann-ivanov-ferber.ru%2Fcatalog%2Fproduct%2Fsobace-serdce-vecnye-istorii%2F%3Futm_source%3Dmindbox%26utm_medium%3Demail%26utm_campaign%3DAktivnayaBazaDrBulgakova15-05-2026%23productType%3Dpaperbook%26promoCode%3DBEGEMOT26)

Все начинается с операции, которая должна была изменить одного. А меняет всех.

[![](https://email-images.mindbox.ru/39d15ed3-003c-4e05-843d-5bfc760db886/5.jpeg)](https://tn-sc.mckx.ru/c/LtooAAAIoJYAwOqu/aR54Bw/ZrLQLGyw50ksCY4u/?u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.mann-ivanov-ferber.ru%2Fcatalog%2Fproduct%2Fzapiski-iunogo-vraca-vecnye-istorii-young-adult%2F%3Futm_source%3Dmindbox%26utm_medium%3Demail%26utm_campaign%3DAktivnayaBazaDrBulgakova15-05-2026%23productType%3Dpaperbook%26promoCode%3DBEGEMOT26)

Поездка в глушь оборачивается чередой испытаний, ошибок и борьбой со страхами.

[![](https://email-images.mindbox.ru/3de194b5-8cb4-426c-810f-8c19ac33684a/2.jpeg)](https://tn-sc.mckx.ru/c/LtooAAAIoJYAwOqu/ah54Bw/onGXNolk972XFSmd/?u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.mann-ivanov-ferber.ru%2Fcatalog%2Fproduct%2Fmaster-i-margarita-young-adult%2F%3Futm_source%3Dmindbox%26utm_medium%3Demail%26utm_campaign%3DAktivnayaBazaDrBulgakova15-05-2026%23productType%3Dpaperbook%26promoCode%3DBEGEMOT26)

Иногда разговор с незнакомцем на скамейке переворачивает все с ног на голову.

body:
#### About Our Contributing Expert

### Sonam Bijani | Data Quality & Governance Leader

[![](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!5937!,w_1100,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F863f4653-b146-4f45-8b5a-a2aa1b09976b_1600x900.png)](https://substack.com/redirect/68733af5-ce07-4fa2-a4b5-76308b7c1ad3?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

Sonam Bijani is a Data Quality & Governance leader focused on building trusted data foundations for AI-ready organisations. With experience across firms like *Eastspring Investments*, *DBS Bank*, and *EY*, she specialises in aligning business and engineering teams on data definitions, ownership, and accountability.

Sonam has led initiatives across implementing data quality frameworks, aligning business and engineering teams on critical data definitions, and embedding governance into the actual flow of data. Her perspective extends naturally into AI. Sonam emphasises that improving AI outcomes is less about better models and more about building stronger data foundations.

> *We actively collaborate with data experts to bring the best resources to a [20,000+ strong community](https://substack.com/redirect/48ba0cc6-6b12-4922-baf1-d60fc7f0bb92?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) of data leaders and practitioners. If you have something to share, reach out!  
>   
> 🫴🏻 Share your ideas and work: [community@moderndata101.com](https://substack.com/redirect/88ef46ec-e827-4bf8-950c-6dde743b4ec0?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)*

###### *\*Note: Opinions expressed in contributions are not our own and are only curated by us for broader access and discussion. All submissions are vetted for quality & relevance. We keep it information-first and do not support any promotions, paid or otherwise!*

---

### Let’s Dive In

[![](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!tElg!,w_1100,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Ff642e723-1eca-4ebe-b4bd-38f05fe738b8_1920x1080.png)](https://substack.com/redirect/e7246544-2404-48e5-8f08-59383eab0ccc?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

Over the last year, most enterprise AI discussions have centered on model capability. Larger context windows, improved reasoning benchmarks, multimodal inputs.

> ### Yet in almost every investment data program I have been involved in, the core bottleneck has NOT been computational power.

It has been semantic clarity.

Large language models, including those developed by OpenAI and Google DeepMind, operate by identifying statistical patterns in language. They do not possess intrinsic awareness of how an organization defines its business concepts. They assume that terms used consistently in text refer to stable underlying meaning.

In an enterprise environment, that assumption is fragile.

---

## The Semantic Fragility of Investment Data

Consider the term *portfolio* in an investment management firm. At first glance, it appears unambiguous. In practice, it is layered.

[![](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!5yCK!,w_1100,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F654055be-b05a-43ec-9186-53686b20a38b_1920x1080.png)](https://substack.com/redirect/b786c17b-afe0-4aa6-bae4-3026303c3124?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

The Anatomy of a Word | Adapted from concepts shared by the Author, curated by Modern Data 101

* In a fund accounting system, *portfolio* may refer to a legal fund vehicle with its own NAV, regulatory classification, and reporting obligations.
* In a front-office order management system, *portfolio* might denote a strategy sleeve or mandate within that fund.
* In performance systems, *portfolio* can represent composites constructed for GIPS

body:
# When Shipping Gets Easy, Choosing Gets Hard

[![](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!tc78!,w_1100,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F46bd1a87-2be9-42cf-a6f2-345a4f6f1cf3_1300x775.png)](https://substack.com/redirect/a7e39eeb-c8f1-4381-927c-f90dba2b4d36?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

What are you going to deliver matters when it’s easy to execute

*Hi, I’m Greg 👋! I write weekly product [essays](https://substack.com/redirect/7b531fee-07fb-4062-a824-bc0b5b6615e4?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ), including system “handshakes”, the expectations for workflow, and the jobs to be done for data. [What is Data Operations?](https://substack.com/redirect/255dfd06-d937-4596-a48a-c85ac0affd67?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) was the first post in the series.*

This week’s toy: Matt Webb has made a fun and shareable way [to collaborate on Markdown files](https://substack.com/redirect/0a934cc8-ddd0-48da-854c-89e9605b7648?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ). (What Google Docs should be doing.)

Edition 292 of this newsletter is here - it’s February 17, 2026.

---

Thanks for reading! Let me know if there’s a topic you’d like me to cover.

---

## **The Big Idea**

*A short long-form essay about data things*

### ⚙️ When Shipping Gets Easy, Choosing Gets Hard

[![](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!tc78!,w_1100,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F46bd1a87-2be9-42cf-a6f2-345a4f6f1cf3_1300x775.png)](https://substack.com/redirect/a7e39eeb-c8f1-4381-927c-f90dba2b4d36?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

Your team can ship 10x more, but your judgement still doesn’t scale.

“Why can’t we move faster?” is the question haunting product teams right now. The usual suspects: tech debt, decision debt, not enough hands. “Not enough resources” or “too many problems, pick one.”

One root cause is cycle time—the need to keep changes atomic, low-risk, and decoupled. Take a small front-end fix. You move through problem identification, investigation, implementation, review, testing, revision, release.

Multiply that by a backlog of “small improvements,” and most of the week disappears into mechanical work. In that world, execution was expensive. Prioritization mattered, but capacity was the visible constraint.

That assumption is breaking. With bounded agent workflows, I can run small implementation tasks in parallel using explicit “skills” and scoped “subagents.” These bots draft changes, generate tests, produce PR notes, and surface risks for review.

They are not magical “Sorcerer’s Apprentice” bots. They do what you tell them—and maybe a bit more. They make mistakes, but they are reliable enough that execution cost is dropping fast.

When execution becomes cheap, weak judgment gets exposed.

### **The bottleneck moved upstream**

[![](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!RfO2!,w_1100,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Fd941d1f5-6275-4cf3-8427-2fb121bdc6ef_1856x780.png)](https://substack.com/redirect/41e359c7-a1fc-44cd-b503-12fbad0b213d?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

Software is not limited by typing speed, or even by agents filling in software Mad Libs on your behalf. Software is limited by decision quality and second-order effects.

* What should exist at all?
* What failure modes are we introducing?
* What complexity are we normalizing?
* What future roadmap options are we quietly closing?

When implementation is expensive, bad prioritization hides behind scarcity. You cannot approve everything.

When execution gets cheap, that buffer disappears.

If your team can generate ten viable changes by noon, t

subject: Brex’s AI Hail Mary — With CTO James Reggio
body:
# Brex’s AI Hail Mary — With CTO James Reggio

In 2024, there was a big question mark around the future of Brex as they [cut 20% of staff among stalled growth](https://substack.com/redirect/e30e6498-c00a-496a-8e98-3112e9fa2dd9?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) with the space becoming increasingly competitive. Fast forward to 2025, Brex has accomplished one of the [most impressive turnarounds](https://substack.com/redirect/2778872b-46c9-4200-a42d-3dffcf99dfca?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ), accelerating sales and passing $500 million in annualized revenue with [European expansion](https://substack.com/redirect/8cd5a535-f380-4767-8899-73f6a89b3c29?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) in sight, dissipating concerns of a dying business. Among the internal changes that led to this successful turnaround was an aggressive shift towards AI adoption and utilization in every aspect of Brex’s business.

In this episode, we sit down with Brex CTO James Reggio to discuss Brex’s culture and how they facilitated an aggressive shift towards a culture of AI fluency in addition to how Brex modernized their tech stack and apply AI agents to streamline their business.

## **Culture**

### Team

Heading into 2024, Brex showed natural signs of a startup scaling up as they continued increasing headcount and expanded org layers to accommodate. However, Brex realized the rate they were scaling the company didn’t match their speed of execution. Addressing this scary truth head on, Brex [laid off 282 people (~20% of the company)](https://substack.com/redirect/b7aa5270-1940-470e-ad03-0f60560af0bc?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ), flattened their org structure, and reduced layers of management with the goal of having leaders “operate closer to the metal” and be less siloed with only a few important cross-company priorities.

[![](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!mqO8!,w_1100,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F519dd245-9dc6-40a9-b868-c0d140d5585e_1536x1024.png)](https://substack.com/redirect/f886ac51-6539-4902-a365-0d3d02103d99?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

[Visualized from “A Message from Pedro” - 1/23/24](https://substack.com/redirect/b7aa5270-1940-470e-ad03-0f60560af0bc?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

Brex realized that speed and execution shouldn’t come at the cost of increasing headcount. Even as Brex scaled up, it can still operate similar to a startup with high-velocity.

In March 2024, Franceschi described this as Brex 3.0: [a new operating model designed to increase intensity and execution quality](https://substack.com/redirect/0336ccc4-3909-4a00-bdf1-7bce17b61fba?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) by making fewer bets, consolidating to one roadmap, and maintaining a release cadence. They doubled down on fostering a high trust and high performance team by promoting from within, bringing employees back in-person to work, and expecting leaders to [operate at all levels](https://substack.com/redirect/7798800a-c819-4d54-b97d-d8a0f463565f?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ).

Brex’s team now consists of ~300 engineers and ~350 across EPD (Engineering, Product, & Design). Their team is split across product domains in addition to infrastructure. Their core product domains are the following:

* Corporate Card
* Corporate Bank Account
* Expense Management
* Travel
* Accounting

In addition to these product teams, Brex has formed smaller specialized teams like their most [recent team of ~10 focused on LLMs](https://substack.com/redirect/9d706195-0b90-4e00-aca3-7441f64200f7?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ). subject: Confessions of a Millennial in Tech
body:
# Confessions of a Millennial in Tech

I’ve been in tech long enough to think I’d already lived through the big shifts.

We went from on-prem to cloud. Then came digital transformation, where every company suddenly needed to become a software company (whether they had any business doing so or not). Entire stacks got rebuilt - .NET stopped feeling inevitable, Python spread everywhere, and everyone got weirdly excited about Next.js. Mobile came in hot (B2B, naturally, is still deciding whether a phone is a real device). Recurring revenue became our SaaS religion. Remote work exploded, then partially un-exploded. Product-led growth rewired how companies scaled.

Each wave felt big. AI feels 10x bigger. And 10x faster.

That speed is the part I can’t quite process. There are days where it genuinely feels like I need a full-time job just to keep up with what’s happening. And even then, I’m not convinced I am. Am I just getting better at being slightly less behind?? Haha.

And that’s really the feeling underneath all of this: behind.

Not “I should probably test that new tool” behind. More like “am I already operating on an outdated mental model?” behind.

There’s also a weird social dynamic to this whole thing. Everyone has a system, a stack, a workflow that supposedly changed their life, saved them from the burnout, and probably whitened their teeth. It creates this illusion that everyone else already knows what’s going on.

So you hesitate to ask basic questions, because it feels like you’re the only dumb one who doesn’t get it.

Which is almost certainly not true. But it feels true. And the result is a lot of fake confidence theater, a lot of noise, and very little shared truth about what’s actually working.

Then there’s the part that’s harder to admit: a lot of what I spent the last decade learning is losing leverage.

Growth, marketing, product management, sales - these used to feel like crafts. You built intuition over years. You learned what great looked like. You got good at pattern recognition. You earned judgment and respect by grinding through it all.

AI is flattening a lot of that.

It’s a weird experience to spend ten years becoming excellent at something only to watch a 22-year-old produce a suspiciously solid version of it in 14 minutes. Not the best version. But enough to make you sit there like, wow, okay then. And you don’t really get to process that shift. There’s no mourning period. You just move on to the next thing, because everything is changing too fast. (and don’t even get me started on how non-tech people are supposed to keep up with any of this - ‘mass adoption’ feels almost comical.)

Which forces a much more uncomfortable question: if your identity was tied to being good at X, what happens when X gets automated?

Now, senior people still have some advantages, but some of the old signals of seniority are getting weaker fast. The hierarchy flattens. The ladder gets weird. Experience still matters, but not in the clean, linear way we got used to.

Honestly, I think that a lot of that is good. A lot of old hierarchies deserved to die. RIP politics and middle-management. Still, it’s disorienting as we are going through it.

And of course, the reward for becoming more efficient is exactly what it has always been: more work. If AI makes you 10x faster, nobody says, “Amazing. Please enjoy your afternoon!” They ask why you’re not doing 10x more. Productivity gains get absorbed immediately by the system, which is very on-brand for tech.

And underneath all of this is the part we really don’t want to talk about: the economics.

If output goes up while the cost of producing that output goes down, what happens to compensation? What happens to leverage? What happens to the premium attached to knowledge work when more of that work becomes abundant? What happens to company structures when fewer people can produce dramatically more?

My guess is the value shifts.

# Nan Ransohoff: Finding Things Out, Double Life, Matriarch, Inputs, Evil, the Beatles

Welcome to a new issue of *Words That Matter*! Each week, we invite a guest curator to share the reading that matters most to them.

Nan Ransohoff ([@nanransohoff](https://substack.com/redirect/b6596dfa-e153-45db-a882-3dbc0552fee3?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)) leads Stripe Climate and founded [Frontier](https://substack.com/redirect/658ecedc-fe3c-4a50-a7dc-198adbfab934?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ), a $1B+ advance market commitment for permanent carbon removal. More broadly, her work focuses on incentive design to help solve important societal problems. Previously she built products at Uber, Nuro and Opower. She was named to the Bloomberg 50 in 2022 and the TIME100 Climate list in 2025.

Nan writes about topics like market shaping for public goods, moral imagination, and San Francisco culture on her [website](https://substack.com/redirect/761891d1-fb54-46e4-b555-d0c91f5d9e12?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) and [Substack](https://substack.com/redirect/d54ee593-88ef-4cf6-b64a-aa7ca4d85061?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ).

Please enjoy these works and words that have mattered to Nan!

## Nan’s Picks

### [The pleasure of finding things out](https://substack.com/redirect/f5b5af61-0ae4-4319-b8a6-1e96936b108d?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) (essay collection)

Richard Feynman

This is a collection of Feynman essays and interviews that are ostensibly about science, but really they’re about much of life – embracing uncertainty, finding the fun and mischief in things, dialing up wonder, exploring big ideas with both intellectual honesty and also a lightness. I forget how I stumbled across these essays originally, but for the past few years I’ve returned to them many times when I’m in need of a mindset ‘tune-up.’ They’ve become sort of medicinal for me – even ~15 minutes with one of them can reliably infuse my brain with a lot more color / texture / energy. (My favorites are:[The pleasure of finding things out](https://substack.com/redirect/c3cc129c-9b1d-405a-80d2-727eab9534dd?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ), [There’s plenty of room at the bottom](https://substack.com/redirect/4cad1588-2c2c-464a-9f84-b16b22341f89?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ), and What is and what should be the role of scientific culture? – but hop around at your leisure!)

---

### [The lives they loved – Regine Weiss Ransohoff](https://substack.com/redirect/bca7bc7c-fd90-4524-b3f8-405243eee78c?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) (essay)

Martha Ransohoff Adler

I’ll start with the obligatory admission that I am obviously biased here: this is a short piece written by my aunt about my grandmother when she died. Even so! I am pretty sure I’d still love this piece even if I didn’t know Regine. It’s a masterclass in capturing the essence of a person. You can feel how fierce, principled, irreverent, brilliant and witty she was, even in just a few short paragraphs. I think about this piece a lot. It makes me wonder what my (hypothetical) daughter would write about me. It forces an almost semi-regular check-in with myself to see if I’m living in a way that feels directionally aligned with who I hope and aspire to be.

---

### [The marriage question: George Eliot’s double life](https://substack.com/redirect/7f7eda3c-ebd1-4906-8a72-32e7ace9e269?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) (book)

Clare Carlisle

This book is responsible for my obsession with George Eliot (yes, yes, I too read Middlemarch and loved it, but this took the love to a new level). Among the many reasons to love Eliot is that she made some insanely bold/risky/controversial life choices by *today’s* standards, let alone for a
