# You're using AI wrong

[![](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!dZ50!,w_1100,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Ff6db6db7-4f20-425f-8ce3-9628f489bfd4_1920x1182.png)](https://substack.com/redirect/eba9269a-bdcc-4b68-907d-c2cd40bdb8a0?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

Photo by [Sen](https://substack.com/redirect/f15a31fa-f34e-4878-98cb-92d33d6029c4?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) on [Unsplash](https://substack.com/redirect/51694042-1151-4b33-82ad-0f51e8a91204?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

*Hi, I’m Greg 👋! I write weekly product [essays](https://substack.com/redirect/5c8c7f45-01dc-4961-8305-cd833791e50f?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ), including system “handshakes”, the expectations for workflow, and the jobs to be done for data. [What is Data Operations?](https://substack.com/redirect/4968d934-6f40-4f4e-8bfe-9ebfd5911712?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) was the first post in the series.*

This week’s toy: a functional LEGO keyboard brick that’s a computer. If you remember the single bricks that showed a '"computer” this is a scaled implementation of that idea: a real computer in the shape of [a square LEGO brick with a slanted front](https://substack.com/redirect/ca39ec48-d1c2-4632-9861-dd6aa7cc4e72?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ). Edition 296 of this newsletter is here - it’s March 16, 2026.

---

Thanks for reading! Let me know if there’s a topic you’d like me to cover.

---

## **The Big Idea**

*A short long-form essay about data things*

### ⚙️ You’re using AI wrong

[![](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!dZ50!,w_1100,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Ff6db6db7-4f20-425f-8ce3-9628f489bfd4_1920x1182.png)](https://substack.com/redirect/e11b63bc-aad8-4e5e-b631-999c13775a05?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

I asked a friend this week what he was building with AI.

“I’m doing some pretty interesting things with ChatGPT,” he said.

I waited for the rest of the sentence, and there wasn’t anything else.

He meant he was searching. Asking questions, getting answers, maybe summarizing an article. He was using a large language model the same way he used Google in 2015, just with better grammar on the output side.

twiI am pretty sure most of the American public believes that “using AI” means typing questions into ChatGPT or Claude and getting slightly better search results. If they are really advanced, they have customized a chatbot to give domain-specific answers, or connected it to their email so it can surface calendar conflicts.

That is not using AI. That is using a chat window.

### **The local maximum**

We’re all used to hearing a message: AI equals chatbot. A chatbot is an application focused on chatting.

So people chat. They ask questions. They get answers. They move on.

What they don’t realize is that behind that chat window sits a system that can help you create software, invent new document formats, build internal tools, generate curriculum for almost any skill, and co-author things that would have taken a team of specialists a year ago.

This is a failure of imagination, not intelligence. People are not dumb, they just don’t have good context for what is possible. When the only frame you have been given is a text box that answers questions, you ask questions.

You do not think to ask it to build you a personal CRM, design a reading tracker, or generate a custom invoice system for your freelance business. (And you should!)

subject: AI Tools for Data Engineers and Data Analysts
body:
# AI Tools for Data Engineers and Data Analysts

Working with different data teams, I’ve observed three distinct groups:

1. **AI avoiders:** Those who rely only on traditional development practices and ignore AI tools entirely
2. **Over-reliant users:** Those who copy-paste everything into ChatGPT for all their tasks
3. **AI enthusiasts:** Those too deep in AI development—constantly experimenting with the latest models and techniques

The optimal approach lies between groups 2 and 3. Developers/Engineers and analysts should:

* Understand AI capabilities and limitations
* Apply AI strategically to appropriate tasks
* Stay informed without getting distracted by every new release

This balanced approach maximizes both speed and quality gains.

In this blogpost, I want to highlight the available list of tools and cover some of the definitions.

> TL;DR:
>
> * Get Cursor IDE.
> * Use Auto mode.
> * Add rules per repo.
> * Add MCP integration for tools you are using.
>
> Don’t worry if something unclear, just use it daily and you will be fine.

## 1. Key Terms (Before Diving into AI Dev Assistants)

Understanding these terms will help you choose the right tools, control costs, and get better results.

### 1.1 LLM (Large Language Model)

An **LLM** is a model trained on huge amounts of text (and sometimes code) that can generate text, answer questions, and follow instructions. When you chat with an AI assistant or ask it to write code, you are talking to an LLM.

[![](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!xdif!,w_1100,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F24c13c8b-4559-4645-8800-6a9ba91f0a9e_936x504.png)](https://substack.com/redirect/20c2f538-b1b0-477e-898d-d8241bf3c7d0?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

**Simple example:** You type “Write a SQL query to get the last 7 days of orders.” The model reads your text and generates SQL. It does not run the query; it only produces the text.

---

### 1.2 LLM Model Providers and Models

A **model provider** is the company or service that hosts and serves the models. You send your prompt to their API and get a response.

[![](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!LREc!,w_1100,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F770e0324-05f1-4df4-94a5-9145d209bb13_650x210.png)](https://substack.com/redirect/3ee24524-a2ed-43ed-8625-7f31f65db5d0?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

Models from the same provider can differ in:

* **Speed** – faster models are usually cheaper and sometimes less capable.
* **Context window** – how much text (and code) they can read at once (e.g. 32K, 200K tokens).
* **Reasoning vs non-reasoning** – see below.

---

### 1.3 Reasoning vs Non-Reasoning Models

**Non-reasoning (standard) models**  
They read your prompt and generate a response in one pass. They are fast and cost less per request. Good for: short answers, simple code, edits, and most day-to-day tasks.

**Reasoning models** (e.g. OpenAI o1, o3; some “thinking” modes)  
They spend extra “thinking” steps before answering. They can be better for hard logic, math, or multi-step planning, but they are slower and **use more tokens** (so they cost more). Use them when you need deeper reasoning, not for every request.

**Practical tip:** For most data work (SQL, dbt, Python, docs), a good non-reasoning model (e.g. Claude 3.5 Sonnet, GPT-4o) is enough. Switch to a reasoning model only when you hit a genuinely hard problem.

---

### 1.4 Tokens

**Tokens** are the units the model uses to read and write text. Roughly:

* 1 token ≈ 4 characters in English, or about ¾ of a word.
* Code and symbols often use more tokens per character.

# Go crazy, folks, go crazy

[![Ozzie Smith](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!0y7j!,w_1100,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F377eb840-784a-4c90-be76-f4268c5dfbaf_1040x1602.jpeg "Ozzie Smith")](https://substack.com/redirect/ee278b0b-7fdc-4636-b4d3-06e60a0854c9?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

The three soundtracks to my life: [This](https://substack.com/redirect/8908b479-e4bb-4103-a0fa-e6944b1c7273?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ), [this](https://substack.com/redirect/1c767e62-e96c-4072-8878-df6cfdbb6172?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ), and [this](https://substack.com/redirect/a65bfb52-52b5-42ab-b382-9097d86e01e5?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ).

Right now, millions of engineers are using AI to do their job. “Top engineers at Anthropic, OpenAI say AI now writes 100% of their code,” [says Fortune](https://substack.com/redirect/b408aa83-f072-407f-8fc0-4db344b0b5c5?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ). Claude is now effectively writing itself, [says the person](https://substack.com/redirect/31a8a0d6-bae7-4970-9438-bff5cc9694a9?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) building Claude.¹ “When AI writes almost all code, what happens to software engineering?,” [asks a software engineer](https://substack.com/redirect/d44ffb54-2f2a-4893-bdb2-4f238062c06a?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ). This is all a very well known phenomenon at this point.²

By contrast, data analysts, who also write a lot of code, are *not* using AI to do their jobs. Though most use chat applications like ChatGPT, a 2025 survey from dbt Labs found that [less than a third](https://substack.com/redirect/9002d43f-e521-4996-a7bb-fc78681516d2?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) are using dedicated development tools. Things may have changed since that survey—it’s from *early* 2025, which was years ago [these days](https://substack.com/redirect/cfb2ff0d-b170-49bf-a641-75fcec3622ef?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)—but by most accounts, AI seems to be upending analysts’ lives much less than it’s upending engineers’.

You could have two theories about this:

1. Analysts do a job that is uniquely hard for AI. We’ve [talked](https://substack.com/redirect/d985fe31-fb0e-4fb5-9134-1c7f23bc8a42?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) about [this](https://substack.com/redirect/cdf920d4-fa78-4ea6-bcce-d80807844c8d?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) theory a lot. Software projects are relatively contained—there is a codebase; there are users who give feedback on what that codebase does; there can be specifications for how you want to update that codebase to improve it; all of these things can be written down. Software is also relatively testable—change the code; push the new button; does it work? Data analysis is neither of these things. To solve an analytical problem, you have to know about a codebase, but also [a business](https://substack.com/redirect/9d2a0b0a-5199-4075-b49c-b6aa65572950?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ), a market, [the thoughts inside of people’s heads](https://substack.com/redirect/0a77d33a-ef0d-4fdb-b4fb-a2f91f01628d?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ), and the location of [nearby electrical substations](https://substack.com/redirect/a90d80dc-2338-4dd4-8423-c8ab96c41172?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ). You [cannot](https://substack.com/redirect/379055f2-61fb-4942-b9e6-fa8f5bb4ff00?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) write all of this down. subject: How These Satellites See What Cameras Can't.
body:
# How These Satellites See What Cameras Can't.

Imagine it’s 2 AM in Eastern Europe. Overcast, no moon in the sky. A column of vehicles is moving across an unlit road. There’s a thick cloud layer sitting at 3,000 feet. To anyone watching from space with a normal camera, that road is empty.

But one satellite in orbit, 400 miles up, fires a radar pulse straight through the cloud cover, through the darkness, and picks up every vehicle on that road. It measures their speed. Their heading. And when one of them pulls off and parks near a structure, it flags the change -- down to the centimeter.

No human looked at this data. An AI read it in seconds.

This technology exists right now. It’s not classified. And [some of it is even free](https://substack.com/redirect/6fbc01f6-dfe3-450e-bdf0-061b560a83fe?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ).

I’ve spent the last few months using open-source intelligence -- including satellite data -- to reconstruct global events like the [Iran strikes](https://substack.com/redirect/9c171161-d095-4150-951f-66c34b7e9005?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) and the [Hormuz crisis](https://substack.com/redirect/3116b426-24f4-482a-afcc-10ce92fb9363?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ). And on the defense and intelligence side of all that, synthetic aperture radar -- SAR -- is foundational to how a lot of it actually works.

Here’s what it is, why it’s about to be everywhere, and why that should make you both excited and a little uneasy.

---

## How It Actually Works

[![](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!U3PT!,w_1100,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F10bf5921-afc7-4106-b587-5095355c0dd8_3840x2160.jpeg)](https://substack.com/redirect/8da61f2c-8a81-4988-9a8a-fbeb1831a9e2?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

Synthetic aperture radar. Satellites fire microwave radar pulses toward the ground and measure what comes back. Pretty standard stuff if you think about it.

But here’s the clever bit. A single radar antenna in space gives you a blurry image. These satellites aren’t static though -- they’re moving, and as they do, they’re collecting thousands of radar returns from slightly different positions. Stitch them all together and you’re basically faking a really long antenna out of pure motion. That’s where the name comes from. Synthetic aperture.

The result is a [25-centimeter resolution reproduction from space](https://substack.com/redirect/6b0dc711-ff9c-4226-bfd4-6da4a8872e04?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ). And what makes SAR different from every electro-optical satellite up there is that it does not care about clouds. Doesn’t care about darkness, smoke, or rain. Optical satellites go completely blind in bad conditions. SAR just punches right through.

Then there’s a technique called InSAR -- Interferometric SAR. You take a radar image of the same spot today, and again several days later, and you start stacking them. What this lets you do is compare tiny phase differences and produce a deformation map -- a record of how much something moved at sub-millimeter precision. Stuff no human eye, not even most physical sensors sitting on the structure, could catch.

The really high-res stuff is either pay-to-play or available only on the defense side. But there’s a satellite constellation in orbit doing this for free, and it’s called [Sentinel-1](https://substack.com/redirect/b31397e7-508c-4d7c-86c8-94f2da2aff88?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ). It covers the planet on a 12-day cycle and anyone can pull it. Pretty fricking powerful for a free tool.  
  
**Watch the full breakdown here:**

[![](https://substackcdn.com/image/youtube/w_728,c_limit/l_youtube_play_qyqt8q,w_120/UKLuei1CnZY)](https://substack.com/redirect/4a9b7ebe-042b-4deb-95a2-310573

# The AI positioning problem for B2B marketers

***Heads-up:** Next week you’ll get an email about how I’m moving my personal writing to [adamgtm.com](https://substack.com/redirect/04de624d-d040-4969-a596-47d0f249b0e1?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) (on beehiiv). There will be an easy opt-out in the flow. This will be the last duplicate post.*

---

Since every B2B company now leads with “AI”, things increasingly look the same to buyers.

It’s a tough job for marketers.

We’ve got to avoid falling into the sea of sameness.

I collected [904 AI product positioning examples](https://substack.com/redirect/d08d0ba9-8e94-4544-90f5-28bafeb8fa64?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) and homepage screenshots to help. Find role models, find gaps, scan it like a buyer.

Explore the **[full gallery here.](https://substack.com/redirect/1422daa0-cd9e-4e0a-8af0-154fc895f270?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)**

[![](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!iC2c!,w_1100,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F315e51a5-6a61-4e30-8759-34d099bdfc0b_1920x935.png)](https://substack.com/redirect/3cbc2ef3-7d16-4e97-99b6-5d891a4cf25a?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

If you find any stand-outs, let me know [in the comments here](https://substack.com/redirect/8c7a45bc-f72f-477d-928e-9a801a2706a4?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ).

**Here are my takeaways (and favorite examples) from analyzing the whole set...**

Generally speaking, I see 10 positioning approaches. Here’s what they mean and how they breakdown amongst AI-Native companies.

[![](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!2Nv7!,w_1100,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F3bbae92e-0043-4e8d-b72f-570033803639_1268x1692.png)](https://substack.com/redirect/aa7794ea-cea9-4576-9dee-fa8934e31c67?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

“AI for [X]” is the default. I saw that in 37% of AI-native companies and a whopping 67% of AI-integrated SaaS companies.

The agentic wave (26%) has three flavors worth noting:

* **“Agentic [Category]”** — 37 companies staple “agentic” onto their category. Agentic CRM. Agentic lakehouse. Agentic procurement. This is “AI for [X]” with a trendier word.
* **“Meet your AI [Role]”** — Bolder. 11x says “Digital workers, Human results.” Lindy says “Meet your first AI employee.” These companies sell teammates, not tools.
* **Agent Platform** — Positioning as the platform for building agents. Writer, Forethought.

# What Stands Out

My role models. The homepages that stopped my scroll all had clarity and confidence.

**Lovable** — “Build something Lovable.” Your company name IS the call to action. Perfect for the Vibe Coding vibes.

[![](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!X2-A!,w_1100,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F38328adc-dc17-47ea-9fdf-56b99a1a64d4_1440x900.jpeg)](https://substack.com/redirect/9abe2292-dd54-4557-8a98-25ae82039556?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

***[Fal.ai](https://substack.com/redirect/65473b57-01df-4d8c-b66d-bde53cec20ba?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)*** — “Generative media platform for developers. Built with fal, loved by all.” They tell you what it is and who it’s for in one line, no “AI” in h1.

[![](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!OM4w!,w_1100,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F0e54b3be-3b32-4dcd-8002-47256728b35a_1440x900.jpeg)](https://substack.com/redirect/2bcaa4f6-f2ce-4247-bf50-bc1fbff59a02?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

AI has dramatically changed how my team operates and we are still early (lots more work to do)…

I built an AI agent that turned a 2-hour task for my accounting team into 5 minutes. And we used this same AI flow across many similar processes (which cut a full day off of the month-end close).

**I just launched a separate newsletter ([CFOpilot](https://substack.com/redirect/103b3bc0-e517-4591-a582-1c2d9b733b45?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)) to write about everything I am learning and building with AI**.

**The below post was shared at **CFOpilot** a few days ago. I got a ton of feedback on how valuable it was, so I wanted to share it here as well.**

# **My 6-Step Process to Building an Accounting AI Agent**

I built our first AI agent to tackle accounting reconciliations (focused on prepaids initially).

Here is the process I ended up with…

[![](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!Lhf-!,w_1100,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F6b899397-f242-4608-b2a7-d3798883a4af_1200x630.png)](https://substack.com/redirect/02b6acd9-8631-44ce-9d05-f66fc299942f?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

An “agent” is essentially the worker that navigates all of these systems and steps to complete a task.

### **Step 1: The “Skill” Itself**
> ***Skill**: A self-contained workflow an agent runs. A system prompt that defines what to do. MCP connectors to the systems it needs. A trigger that kicks it off. A config that drives the behavior. You build it once and it runs forever.*

Every skill has a SKILL.md file. The skill defines the inputs, workflows, rules, output, edge cases, etc. My prepaid skill is ~200 lines.

You’re not writing a prompt every time you run it. You’re writing it once. And then updating it if/when something changes.

### **Step 2: The Config File**

My config (YAML file) contains:

- Prepaid GL account codes

- Vendor → coding map

- Materiality threshold

- Partial-month convention

- Routing: who gets pinged, in which channel

When something changes, you edit the config (not the skill**).**

This is one thing I was doing wrong before. I was dumping everything into a prompt (or a skill). Every time something changed, I would have to update the skill and re-do it.

Having a separate config file with the stuff that might change breaks things up so it’s easier to maintain. It’s like why you don’t put your entire model and all the components in one giant tab or make Excel model formulas huge.

Putting everything in one skill file also makes it so you can’t reuse your skill in other recons, entities, etc because it contains the exact detail for one prepaid recon process. To m

Good news, but not that simple

Dear Reader,

States of emergency became a recurring tool in the fight against organized crime across Latin America and the Caribbean in 2025. While these measures appear to have produced positive results in some cases, such as Jamaica’s 40% drop in homicides, their impact has been far less effective elsewhere. In Ecuador, for example, the government’s militarized response to organized crime triggered new waves of violence.

Although the region as a whole recorded a decline in homicides, that statistic only tells part of a complex story.

**InSight Crime’s donor-exclusive event** on March 26 will examine organized crime dynamics in each country in the region in depth, and discuss what they could mean for the months ahead.

# Not Another Dev Tool

**A special announcement today from my incredible spouse, who is on the hunt for a CTO and cofounder.**

**Marrying her was the best decision I ever made. Starting a company with her may be the best one you make!**

---

Once upon a time, I saw the Komodo dragons in their natural habitat. They were majestic, imposing and the chill they sent down my spine was unforgettable. I am no dragonologist, but a friend and I decided to meet up midway, and that landed us on the Komodo island.

For me, it’s the adventures that give life its magic and the most epic ones start with companions who expand our worlds and draw us to unexpected wonders.

Today, I am seeking a partner to embark on the ultimate commercial adventure: entrepreneurship.

Perhaps you are about to team up with another developer to build another dev tool, but ***let me open the door to a whole new world for you***. If this goes well, we’ll spend the next decade together with an exceptional team of fellow adventurers to push the frontier of a real industry.

### **You might be a good fit if you are:**

1. Based in NYC
2. Already committed to starting a company
3. As good at your craft (ML+data) as I am at mine (see below)
4. Open-minded but decisive
5. Ambitious; our approach will be frontier and radical, not midwit or marginal
6. Down for a 10-year adventure, which may or may not involve riches or glory, but will definitely involve great people and honorable work

### **About me:**

1. I am 10 years out of college, had some big responsibilities professionally, and am now also raising a toddler with Jordan!
2. As a private equity investor for 7 years, I evaluated hundreds of companies (and founders). My portfolio companies exceed $5bn in total valuation, ranging widely from $3mm to $2bn. On this adventure, I developed clarity of thought, a sense for order of magnitude and taste in people
3. As an operator in recent years, I defined strategies, closed deals, opened new markets, ran payroll, delivered hiring and firing decisions, etc. On this adventure, I recognized how much I have to give. One startup I coached received a ~100% valuation increase after I rebuilt the narrative and told them the numbers to ask
4. Over the years, I earned the trust of some people who think the world of me
5. I go very deep into very niche topics, in order to do that I have a high bar for what’s worthwhile; I will work 24/7 when called for, but not 996 every week
6. I consider the ultimate job of a CEO to defy gravity, as most companies see their upside shrink overtime. I have watched this happen up close twice, painfully. If I get this right, it will not be me alone - although I do have great instincts - but because our trust in each other keeps us honest, in perspective and relentless

### **The idea space:**

**You may have guessed, dear smart reader, that if the idea space was “sexy” I would have put it in the first paragraph. But remember, I am looking to expand worlds (yours and mine); you don’t need to be an insider because you have me.**

This is a multi-trillion dollar industry with highly specialized talent. It was Franz Kafka’s day job and the core engine of Warren Buffett’s empire. High walls surround it but the people inside are generous, smart and fun!

Welcome to the world of insurance.

I have invested in insurance companies and operated within insurance companies as General Manager and VP of Finance. We won’t be selling insurance policies. We’ll solve structural, heavy-lifting, legacy tech debt that can build us a data moat to move the entire industry to the agentic era. Few trillion-dollar industries have this opportunity still on the table.

I have a hypothesis and people to call; we will work together on the strategy, product and plan. And if you have a better idea outside insurance, let’s pressure-test both.

**Interested? Use this [form](https://substack.com/redirect/22fceb10-748e-4353-a49a-9f9ae7f742ce?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkX

body:
# The AI Acqui-Hire Wave

Tomasz Tunguz

Venture Capitalist at [Theory Ventures](https://6a50e11d.click.convertkit-mail2.com/r8uklqk5nptoh34w8krc2hdnn8n66s7hwl39x/9qhzhnhd0x57g7t9/aHR0cHM6Ly90aGVvcnkudmVudHVyZXM=)

Scale AI sold for $14.8 billion.[1](#fn:1) Character.AI for $2.5 billion.[2](#fn:2) Inflection for $650 million.[3](#fn:3) They represent a tiny fraction of the market.

[![AI Acqui-Hires by Year](https://res.cloudinary.com/dzawgnnlr/image/upload/w_1512,h_850,c_fill,g_auto,q_auto,f_auto/ueq2i4nmgon2o9hj7wtl)](https://6a50e11d.click.convertkit-mail2.com/r8uklqk5nptoh34w8krc2hdnn8n66s7hwl39x/owhkhqhwpnqzrxcv/aHR0cHM6Ly9yZXMuY2xvdWRpbmFyeS5jb20vZHphd2dubmxyL2ltYWdlL3VwbG9hZC9xX2F1dG8sZl9hdXRvL3VlcTJpNG5tZ29uMm85aGo3d3Rs)

From 2020 to 2025, there were 5,700 AI & ML acquisitions. Only 21% disclosed a deal value. The remaining 4,500 share a pattern : small teams absorbed into larger companies. No fanfare. No valuation headlines. Just talent migrating from startup to incumbent.

It’s cheaper to buy a team than to compete for hires or build from scratch.

[![Top AI Acquirers : Disclosed vs Undisclosed Deals](https://res.cloudinary.com/dzawgnnlr/image/upload/w_1512,h_1702,c_fill,g_auto,q_auto,f_auto/wdsgrw532ppkfdjrm7hl)](https://6a50e11d.click.convertkit-mail2.com/r8uklqk5nptoh34w8krc2hdnn8n66s7hwl39x/z2hghnhen7lg3nhp/aHR0cHM6Ly9yZXMuY2xvdWRpbmFyeS5jb20vZHphd2dubmxyL2ltYWdlL3VwbG9hZC9xX2F1dG8sZl9hdXRvL3dkc2dydzUzMnBwa2ZkanJtN2hs)

The buyers are surprising. Accenture leads with 21 AI acquisitions, only three disclosed. Apple follows with 17, just two disclosed. Google & Microsoft rank far lower.

The 75th percentile deal size tripled from $82M in 2020 to $248M in 2025. The urgency behind developing a strong AI strategy is rising.

Thanks to the companies that made the **[AI x GTM Summit](https://substack.com/redirect/b769cee2-1910-43d0-b054-436cf02d3a58?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)** possible! [![](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!fz3G!,w_1100,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Fde6b0dc3-356f-441e-b70f-9426e0c36bc8_2279x1231.jpeg)](https://substack.com/redirect/3d209543-7a9d-419c-b5c1-5205b9055df4?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

---

#### The Alpha Is in the Niche Signals

Publicly available, third-party signals are becoming commoditized.

Job postings, website visits, LinkedIn engagement. Everyone’s tracking these now. They’re better than nothing, but [the real alpha is in niche signals](https://substack.com/redirect/65ec252c-0ec5-4289-b976-344f016b3183?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ).

At the AI x GTM Summit, [Soham Maniar](https://substack.com/redirect/2fc86197-7dd0-4b02-993d-1e933474e8ee?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) (a modern RevOps ninja) shared what actually works in [signal-based selling](https://substack.com/redirect/16fb42f9-64b7-4abb-8b0c-64e1ac876910?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ). Soham is one of those RevOps people who makes the job feel creative and fun while still being rigorous. He’s currently at Nominal.io and has built signal engines at companies like Weaviate and others.

Our conversation covered how to think about signals, where the real value is, and how to operationalize all of this without drowning in noise.

Here’s what we covered:

* **Setting the stage: TAM → ICP → SBM**
* **AI-enabled company tiering** (custom ICP)
* **The three-circle overlap** (ICP + engagement + readiness)
* **Niche signals are the alpha** (plus real examples)
* **Timing matters more than copy**
* **How to find the right signals for your business**
* **Who owns this?** (RevOps, GTM engineering, SDR leaders)
* **Operationalizing signals without creating noise**

Follow [Soham](https://substack.com/redirect/4db1d11b-e336-49ab-a207-1a0c27978a17?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ) on LinkedIn! He’s a legend.

# Import AI 457: AI stuxnet; cursed Muon optimizer; and positive alignment

Welcome to Import AI, a newsletter about AI research. Import AI runs on arXiv, cappuccinos, and feedback from readers. If you’d like to support this, please subscribe.

[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..qyZyktqIwEuNC-mwwnv2pq_AahJAunlCKzPuZpdngfk?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=198183721)

**Stuxnet before Stuxnet:**  
*…Fast16 bugs software likely used in weapons programs…*  Here’s a fascinating investigation of a ~20+ year old computer virus called fast16.sys. This software is interesting because it “selectively targets high-precision calculation software, patching code in memory to tamper with results. By combining this payload with self-propagation mechanisms, the attackers aim to produce equivalent inaccurate calculations across an entire facility.”  If any of you have read the Three Body Problem, this might sound familiar - in that (fictional) book, aliens intent on taking over the Earth use a technology called a Sophon to disrupt high-energy physics experiments all over the world, making it impossible for humanity to advance certain types of science.  

**More details on the virus:** When the researchers at SentinelOne did their teardown of the virus they found something quite unusual: “Most patched patterns correspond to standard x86 code used for hijacking or influencing execution flow. One injected block is different. It’s a larger and complex sequence of Floating Point Unit instructions dedicated to precision arithmetic and scaling values in internal arrays. This code is a standalone mathematical calculation function unrelated to code flow hijacking or any other typical malicious code injection.”  Further investigation deepened the mystery: “We converted the patching rules into hexadecimal YARA signatures and ran them against a large, period‑appropriate corpus. The results showed a very low hit rate: fewer than ten files matched two or more patterns. Those matches, however, shared a clear theme. They were precision calculation tools in specialised domains such as civil engineering, physics and physical process simulations.”  

**Targeted tools:** “The strongest overlaps point to three high-precision engineering and simulation suites from the mid-2000s: LS-DYNA 970, PKPM, and the MOHID hydrodynamic modeling platform, all used for scenarios like crash testing, structural analysis, and environmental modeling,” they write. “LS-DYNA in particular has been cited in public reporting on Iran’s suspected violations of Section T of the JCPOA, in studies of computer modeling relevant to nuclear weapons development… by introducing small but systematic errors into physical‑world calculations, the framework could undermine or slow scientific research programs, degrade engineered systems over time or even contribute to catastrophic damage.”  

**Why this matters - this is how a superintelligence might prevent others from coming into existence**: fast16 is a subtle, hard-to-find bug which has been designed to degrade an actor’s ability to do certain types of science. You might imagine that a superintelligence could view “AI non-proliferation” as being just as important as nuclear states view “nuclear non-proliferation”.

[Sign up](https://every.to/emails/click/277e89a96182734274b33414175c1613d4cb600b7e9db7a8ecf343238a13d945/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiVmliZSBDaGVjazogT3B1cyA0LjjigJRBbnRocm9waWMgU2hvdWxk4oCZdmUgUm91bmRlZCBVcCB0byA1IiwicG9zdF9pZCI6NDI3NywicG9zdF90eXBlIjoicG9zdCIsInVybCI6Imh0dHBzOi8vZXZlcnkudG8vYWNjb3VudCIsInBvc2l0aW9uIjo2fQ==) to get it in your inbox.*

---

Anthropic is back.

After a year of riding Claude Code into the rest of knowledge work, the lab hit a rough patch: [Opus 4.7](https://every.) was hard to love, and OpenAI’s [Codex desktop app](https://every.) pulled even devoted Claude users from our team to GPT models. Opus 4.8, out today, has us running back—for the model, if not the app around it. It tops our Senior Engineer Benchmark and our writing tests at once, and it’s the first Anthropic release in a year we’d reach for across coding, prose, and everyday work.

The big insights from our testing:

- **Best on senior-engineer coding.** At extra-high effort, Opus 4.8 scored 63 on our Senior Engineer Benchmark, versus 62 for GPT-5.5 and 33.5 for Opus 4.7. At lower effort settings, the score drops significantly.
- **The strongest writing model we’ve tested.** Opus 4.8 at high effort scored 79.6, ahead of Sonnet 4.6 (74.5), GPT-5.5 (73), and Opus 4.7 (63), with fewer AI tells than any non-Claude model.
- **Best one-shot PowerPoint we’ve seen.** On our Every Consulting Benchmark, Opus 4.8 produced a well-designed deck that told a clear story—something most models still can’t do.
- **The model is stronger than the app.** Opus 4.8 is good enough to make us want to live in Claude, but the split between Chat, Code, and Cowork keeps Codex as the better daily harness.

The full [Vibe Check](https://every.to/emails/click/277e89a96182734274b33414175c1613d4cb600b7e9db7a8ecf343238a13d945/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiVmliZSBDaGVjazogT3B1cyA0LjjigJRBbnRocm9waWMgU2hvdWxk4oCZdmUgUm91bmRlZCBVcCB0byA1IiwicG9zdF9pZCI6NDI3NywicG9zdF90eXBlIjoi

# Join Webinar: Deep Tech Post Series A

You’re invited to an exclusive closed-format session hosted by Beyond Earth Ventures:

**“Beyond the VC Playbook: Corporate Strategy for Deep Tech Post Series A”**

**Register here:** [https://luma.com/c394drb3](https://substack.com/redirect/e001ea88-ea80-4063-9d0b-cec341b60f63?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

**🗓 Date:** Thursday, April 23

**🕐 Time:**

* 🇸🇬 Singapore — 11:00 PM
* 🇬🇧 London — 4:00 PM
* 🇺🇸 San Francisco — 8:00 AM

About **Beyond Earth Ventures**:

Beyond Earth Ventures is a U.S.-based deep tech fund backing the pioneers building the next industrial frontier — on Earth and in Space. Their focus is on the core physical domains of the future: space-tech, energy, robotics, and advanced computing.

[![](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!pp5X!,w_1100,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F4fd588b8-9ab9-4532-a79c-4f4264860317_1248x832.png)](https://substack.com/redirect/f0c2465b-b18f-40fa-838b-1708e24f7012?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

**Speakers:**

**Alexandra Vidyuk** — Founding Partner & CEO, Beyond Earth Ventures. Physicist, ex-Banker, ex-FinTech Entrepreneur, Karman Pioneer, Advisor at Renaissance Philanthropy. Alexandra brings a rare combination of scientific depth and financial markets experience to deep tech investing.

**Nick Dimitriou** — Advisor, Beyond Earth Ventures & Partner at J Goodwin & Co. With 20 years in corporate law, M&A, and capital raising focused on deep tech and frontier technology, Nick has structured some of the most complex transactions in the sector.

**Why this matters:**

Deep tech companies face a unique inflection point after Series A. At this stage, success is no longer defined by access to venture capital alone, but by the ability to design and execute a coherent corporate strategy — one that integrates capital, partnerships, and long-term positioning.

Yet most founders and investors in deep tech remain locked into a single mental model, underutilising the strategic frameworks that are quietly driving the biggest outcomes across space, robotics, energy, and advanced computing.

**In this exclusive session, we will cover:**

* Why traditional VC logic evolves for deep tech companies post Series A — and how leading founders rethink corporate strategy at this stage
* Venture debt & structured financing — as strategic tools to scale without unnecessary dilution, and where they fit within a broader company strategy
* M&A as a strategic pathway — how acquisitions, defence primes, industrial players, and sovereign capital are shaping outcomes in deep tech, and how to position accordingly
* Secondary markets — how founders, LPs, and GPs are integrating liquidity into long-term strategic planning

What the next 24 months look like for corporate strategy in deep tech

**This webinar is for you if:**

* You are a deep tech founder raising beyond Series A and want to think beyond funding rounds towards long-term strategy
* You are an investor or family office looking to understand how value is actually created and realised in deep tech
* You are an LP evaluating exposure to frontier technology funds
* You are a fund manager or M&A professional working with capital-intensive technology companies
* You want to understand how the most sophisticated players are structuring and positioning deep tech companies today

Register here: [https://luma.com/c394drb3](https://substack.com/redirect/e001ea88-ea80-4063-9d0b-cec341b60f63?j=eyJ1IjoiNndtMGMifQ.FKZnV4yDO9r1W3mXiFPvoTkXx7p4iMXPKOi9UqQpNhQ)

Seats are limited. This is a closed-format session.

We look forward to having you.

[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9zcGFjZWFtYml0aW9uLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9zdWJzY3JpYmU_dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1wb3N0JnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj1lbWFpbC1jaGVja291dCZuZXh0PWh0dHBzJTNBJTJGJTJGc3BhY2VhbWJpdGlvbi5zdWJzdGFjay5
